language: 中文字段说明；官方接口名称、签名、代码和原文保留英文

scope.excluded: 未合并网络搜索、同名 Stone 项目、未在这两个目录中出现的第三方实现。
scope.sourceRule: 所有官方能力、函数、参数、返回值和说明均以 D:\Data 下两个目录的 index.json/HTML 为证据；推断字段单独标注。

evidenceModel.official: 页面标题、官方原文、HTML 小节、Synopsis、参数方向、参数表、返回信息、示例代码。
evidenceModel.derived: operationClass、mcpExposure、检索字段和适配器建议，是为了 Agent 编排而增加的推断/工程字段，不是 CAREL 官方函数。
evidenceModel.missing: 资料没有给出 HTTP REST/MCP 服务端点、官方 JSON Schema 或电脑端 Structured Text 远程调用协议；因此控制器端库函数标为“需要适配器”。

mcpAdapterGuidance.purpose: 把官方资料组织为可检索知识库；推荐由外部 MCP Server 调用本机 SToneCLI 或读取工程/设备适配器。

desktopIronPython.runtime: IronPython，官方资料说明支持 Python 3.4；STone IDE 自带运行时，不要求另装 CPython。
desktopIronPython.scriptArgs: -a/--script-args；第一个 sys.argv 元素是脚本路径。

cli.wrapperRule: MCP 工具可以将 command、参数、工作目录和退出码封装为结构化结果；不要把 CLI 命令名扩写成未在资料中出现的 REST API。
cli.mutatingOperations: build、unit-tests 连接/下载、export-workspace 输出、license 激活均应记录路径、目标、参数和退出码。

controllerStructuredText.rule: SToneAPI 页面是控制器应用内可使用的 Structured Text 库，不等于从电脑端直接调用的远程 API。
adapterInputs: 真实运行时返回或事件
controllerStructuredText.default: 优先只读；写入变量、修改网络、服务、文件、固件和重启必须由上层适配器实施显式确认。

officialPages.title: About
officialPages.officialContent:
About STone IDE provides a set of APIs designed to allow users to automate common tasks such as building projects, updating libraries, and downloading to a target, programmatically.
In this documentation, detailed information are provided about these APIs, including the parameters they accept, their return values and sample code snippets to demonstrate their usage.
These APIs can be used within a Python script, which is then executed by SToneCLI.exe via the command:
SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f C:/Path/to/script/example.py Note:
The Python runtime is IronPython, which is a .NET implementation of the Python programming language.
This differs from the standard CPython runtime, but users do not need to install anything other than STone IDE to use these APIs.
The Python version supported is 3.4 (Documentation)
To add external modules append them to sys.path
APIs Overview Below is an overview of the APIs in UML diagram:
APIs usually have a return boolean value, useful to check if the call was successful.
It is recommended to read the documentation in the following order:
stone Solution Project Target Watch Task Example First create a python script which uses the STone APIs.
Python script example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (set_point, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MySetPoint") # Read from variable MySetPoint (value, result) = set_point.ReadValue() print(value) # Stops pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() Then execute it with SToneCLI:
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\CAREL\STone" SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f C:/Path/to/script/example.py Command options iron-python command accepts the following options:
-f, --python-file The path to the python script file to be executed, required. -a, --script-args The arguments to be passed to the python script, optional.
First argument is always the given script path. Example of arguments usage: IronPython script:
import sys print(sys.argv) CLI call:
SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f .\script.py -a first second "third argument" Output:
['.\\script.py', 'first', 'second', 'third argument'] SToneCLI exit codes for iron-python command Exit Code Description 0 No errors from python runtime (e.g. No exceptions). -1 Invalid STone license. -2 Python file not found. -3 Python exception.

officialPages.title: stone
officialPages.officialContent:
stone object This is the entrypoint for all the APIs.
stone is an object that includes within it two other classes: Solution and Target.
The stone object is already present when running the python script, so it doesn’t need to be created (no need to import a module). It is simply called by its name:
stone.Solution.Save() Fields Field Data type Description Solution class The currently open STone solution Target class Contains all the API to manage a target

officialPages.title: Solution
officialPages.officialContent:
Solution class This class represent a STone solution.
Solution is part of the stone object which is already present when running the python script.
Solution is an object that includes within it the class Projects.
Projects is an array with all the projects of the solution (see more in the “Project” page).
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") For obtain a valid STone solution, you could call the method CreateNewSolution:
solution = stone.Solution basedir = 'c:/path/to/your/solution' sln_name = 'TestSolution' tmpl_name = 'BaseProject' # Create a new solution result, sln_file = solution.CreateNewSolution(basedir, sln_name, tmpl_name) # Check the result if result.IsSuccessful: print(sln_file) # Output: c:\path\to\your\solution\TestSolution\TestSolution.stone solution.Open(sln_file) else: # Try to log something print('Creation error:%s' % result.Errors[0].Description) Fields Field Data type Description Projects Array[Project] List of all projects contained in the currently open solution. ActiveSolutionConfiguration SolutionConfiguration The current active solution configuration of the currently open solution. SolutionConfigurations Array[SolutionConfiguration] The list of solution configurations of the currently open solution. Example: Since Projects is a list, you can cycle it with a for.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": # ... Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
Open(solutionPath)Description:
Open and loads a STone solution.
The solution must be opened before calling any other methods like save, compile, etc…
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description solutionPath string The full path of the “.stone” solution file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Solution.stone” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") Close()Description:
Close the currently open STone solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Close the stone solution stone.Solution.Close() Save()Description:
Save the currently open STone solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Save the stone solution stone.Solution.Save() SetActiveProject(projectName)Description:
Set projectName as the Active project of the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project contained it the currently open solution.
e.g. “pCOProject1” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Set "pGD1Prj1" as the active project stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("pGD1Prj1") CreateNewProject(templateName, baseDir, projectName)Description:
Create a new project starting from a project template.
The new project will be created in the folder specified by baseDir with projectName as its name.
templateName can be one of the following:
(Note that related plugins must be installed)
“BaseProject” “EmptyProject” “pCOProject” “pGD1Prj” “SevenSegmentsPrj” Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description templateName string The name of the template on which the project is to be based.
e.g. “BaseProject” baseDir string The absolute path in which to create the project.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\” projectName string The name to give to the new project. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Create a new project named "MyProjectName" based on "BaseProject" stone.Solution.CreateNewProject("BaseProject", "C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Project\\", "MyProjectName") CreateNewSolution(baseDir, name, templateName = "BaseProject")Description:
Create a solution with a template project, the solution name is specified by the parameter name. The new solution will be created under the directory baseDir. You should be aware that a folder with the same name with the solution will be created in baseDir.
The project type is specified by the parameter templateName, which is just same usage with the parameter in CreateNewProject. The possible values will be like following: (Note that related plugins must be installed)
“BaseProject” “EmptyProject” “pCOProject” “pGD1Prj” “SevenSegmentsPrj” Returns:
A tuple with (IResult, string), which gives errors in IResult member and the solution path in string member
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description baseDir string The absolute path in which to create the solution.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\” name string The name of the solution. templateName string The name of the template on which the project is to be based.
e.g. “BaseProject” Example:
solution = stone.Solution # Create a new solution result, sln_file = solution.CreateNewSolution( 'c:/your/solution', 'TestSolution', 'BaseProject' ) if result.IsSuccessful: print(sln_file) else: print(result.Errors[0].Description) AddExistingProject(fileName)Description:
Adds an existing project to the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description fileName string The absolute path of the “.stprj” project file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Project.stprj” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Add "ExistingProject" to solution stone.Solution.AddExistingProject("C:\\Path\\To\\Other\\Solution\\ExistingProject\\ExistingProject.stprj") RemoveProject(projectName, delete = false)Description:
Removes an existing project from the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project contained it the currently open solution.
e.g. “pCOProject1” delete bool If true, delete the project folder. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Remove "ExistingProject" from solution stone.Solution.RemoveProject("ExistingProject") Build()Description:
Compiles the currently open solution.
Returns:
Returns a Result object. Result.IsSuccessful = True if successful and there is no build error, false otherwise and lists “Result.Errors”, “Result.Warning”, “Result.Messages” if any.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Build the solution stone.Solution.Build() SetActiveSolutionConfiguration(solutionConfiguration)Description:
Sets the active solution configuration.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if configuration does not exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description solutionConfiguration SolutionConfiguration The solution configuration to set as the active solution configuration.
Tip: SolutionConfigurations field of Solution class is a list of all the available solution configurations. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Sets Debug as the active solution configuration for configuration in stone.Solution.SolutionConfigurations: if configuration.Name == "Debug": stone.Solution.SetActiveSolutionConfiguration(configuration)

officialPages.title: Project
officialPages.officialContent:
Project class This class represent a STone project within a solution.
Project is part of the Solution class. Solution contains an array of all the projects in the STone solution (see more in the “Solution” page).
Note: Open libraries in the solution are projects.
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution, and get the desired project from the Projects array contained in the Solution class:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": # ... Fields Field Data type Description Name string The name of the project. (Read-Only) e.g. “pCOProject1” Path string The absolute path of the project file. (Read-Only) e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Project.stprj” Files Array[string] The list of all absolute paths of all the user files used by the project. (Read-Only)
Note: This does not includes generated and system files. e.g. [“C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Main.st”, …] ActiveProjectConfiguration ProjectConfiguration The current active project configuration. ProjectConfigurations Array[ProjectConfiguration] The list of project configurations. IsLibrary bool True if the project is a library. (Read-Only) Version string The version of the project. (Read-Only) e.g. “1.2.3” Author string The author of the project. Vendor string The vendor of the project. IsActive bool True if the project is the active project of the solution. (Read-Only) GenerateMetadataFile bool If true generate project metadata file on build. Example: Search for open libraries and close them.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for open libraries and close them for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.IsLibrary: project.CloseProject() # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
AddFile(sourceFilePath, relativeDestinationPath = '', link = false, overwrite = false)Description:
Adds an existing file to the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if file already exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description sourceFilePath string The full path of the file to be added.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\File\file.st” relativeDestinationPath string The project relative destination path in which to add the file.
If empty the file will be added to the root of the project folder. (Default: “”) Tip: GetFolderRelativePaths API returns a list of all the project folders e.g. “Sources\Programs” link bool If true, the file will not be copied to the folder (linked file). (Default: false) overwrite bool If true, if a file with the same name already exists, it is overwritten. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and add Main.st file to Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() RemoveFile(filePath)Description:
Removes a file from the project.
Note: The file will be deleted.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and remove Main.st file from Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.RemoveFile("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\MyProjectName\\Sources\\Programs\\Main.st") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() ExcludeFileFromProject(filePath)Description:
Excludes a file from the project. Note: The file will not be deleted.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and exclude Main.st file from Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.ExcludeFileFromProject("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\MyProjectName\\Sources\\Programs\\Main.st") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() RenameFile(filePath, newName, overwrite = false)Description:
Renames a file of the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file. e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” newName string The new name to give to the file. overwrite bool If true, if a file with the same name already exists, it is overwritten. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Rename all "Main.st" files to "NewName.st" for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for file in project.Files: if file.endswith("Main.st"): project.RenameFile(file, "NewName.st", True) # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() AddLibrary(stlibPath)Description:
Add a library (.stlib file) to the project.
Returns:
The full path to the newly added library on success, otherwise an empty string.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description stlibPath string The full path of the “.stlib” library package file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Lib\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() CloseProject()Description:
Closes the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for open libraries and close them for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.IsLibrary: project.CloseProject() # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() GetOrCreateLibsFolder()Description:
Returns the absolute path of the “Libs” folder of the project.
If the folder does not exist it will be created.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Libs”
Example:
import os # Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Update lib IAQ from version 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for subdir, dirs, libs in os.walk(project.GetOrCreateLibsFolder()): for lib in libs: if "IAQ_v.1.0.0" in lib: project.RemoveFile(lib) project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.2.0.0.stlib") stone.Solution.Save() GetLibsNames(getOpened = true, getClosed = true, withVersion = true)Description:
Returns a list of all the libraries of the project.
e.g. [“IAQ_v.1.0.0”, “SystemMenu_v.1.0.1”]
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description getOpened bool If true, open libraries are included in the list. (Default: true) getClosed bool If true, closed libraries are included in the list. (Default: true) withVersion bool If true, libraries ends with version (e.g. “IAQ_v.1.0.0”) else includes only the name (e.g. “IAQ”). (Default: true) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search libs in all project for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for lib in project.GetLibsNames() # ... GetFolderRelativePaths()Description:
Returns all relative paths of user project folders.
Note: This does not includes reserved folders.
e.g. [“Gui”, “Images”, “Sources”, “Gui\Actions”, “Gui\CustomMasks”, “Sources\Programs”, …]
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Loop through all folders contained in Sources\\ folder for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for folder in project.GetFolderRelativePaths(): if folder.startswith("Sources\\"): # ... GetOutputDir()Description:
Returns the path to the output directory of the build.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Output\Resource1\Configuration1”
Example:
import os bin_files = [] # Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Populate bin_files with all paths to application bin files for project in stone.Solution.Projects: stone.Solution.SetActiveProject(project.Name) stone.Solution.Build() bin_files.append(os.path.join(project.GetOutputDir(), 'flash.bin')) SetActiveProjectConfiguration(projectConfiguration)Description:
Sets the active project configuration.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if configuration does not exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectConfiguration ProjectConfiguration The project configuration to set as the active project configuration.
Tip: ProjectConfigurations field of Project class is a list of all the available project configurations. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Sets Debug as the active project configuration for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for configuration in project.ProjectConfigurations: if configuration.Name == "Debug": project.SetActiveProjectConfiguration(configuration)

officialPages.title: Project Configuration
officialPages.officialContent:
ProjectConfiguration class This class represent a configurations of a STone project within a solution.
They are the same configuration that can be found on Build configuration view of project.
Project is part of the Solution class.
Solution contains an array of all the projects in the STone solution (see more in the “Solution” page).
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution, and get the desired project from the Projects array contained in the Solution class:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": project.ActiveProjectConfiguration.Debug = True # ... Fields Field Data type Description Name string The name of the project configuration. NoLogo bool If true, suppress the display of startup banner and information message. Debug bool If true, enable debugger information on object file (breakpoint support). Coverage bool If true, enable code coverage information on object file. NoOpt bool If true, disable code optimization. NoOptIO bool If true, disable IO optimization. SubrangeCheckEditors bool If true, emit Subrange limits check instructions during Read operations in Protocols, NFC, etc.. SkipApplicationSigning bool If true, skip application signing. InheritMethodVisibility bool If true, inherit method visibility rather than using default visibility (protected). RepeatUntilExitsOnFalse bool If true, the REPEAT/UNTIL loop will exit when condition evaluation returns FALSE, behaving like a DO/WHILE loop. LongStrings bool If true, enable the usage of Long Strings, with length over 255. Configuration string The project ST configuration. Resource string The project ST resource. CustomFileDirectories string Custom file directories. PreprocessorDefinitions string Preprocessor definitions. UserParameters string User parameters. PreBuildCommandLine string Pre-build events command line. PostBuildCommandLine string Post-build events command line. Example: Disable InheritMethodVisibility on MyProject.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Disable InheritMethodVisibility on MyProject for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": project.ProjectConfiguration.InheritMethodVisibility = False # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Close()

officialPages.title: Target
officialPages.officialContent:
Target class This class contains all the APIs to manage a target, so it is possible to download, restart the target, read from and write to variables, use device recovery, etc…
Target class is part of the stone object which is already present when running the python script.
Except for device recover, the APIs works for both pc simulator and physical controller.
Fields Field Data type Description Watches Array[Watch] List of all successfully created watches. Tasks (Array[Task], Result) Tuple with a list of all tasks present in the target and a result instance. The list of all tasks is a Task instance. The result instance containing some information if the list cannot be retrieved. ActiveTask (Task, Result) Tuple with a the active tasks present in the target and a result instance. The active tasks are in a Task instance. The result instance containing some information if the list cannot be retrieved. WorkingDirectory string String with the current Working Directory of the simulator process Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
StartSimulator()Description:
Starts the “PC-Simulator” target with the settings of “STone IDE > Tools > Options > Simulation”.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() StopSimulator()Description:
Stops the “PC-Simulator” target
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Stops the pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() Connect(connectionString)Description:
Opens a connection to the target via the specified connectionString.
Returns:
True if successful and connected, false otherwise or if a connection already exists.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description connectionString string The Connection string to the target.
e.g. “TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122” or “Serial,COM11,1152008N1,248” for serial. Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") Disconnect()Description:
Closes the currently open connection.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Disconnect from the pc-simulator stone.Target.Disconnect() Restart()Description:
Restarts the target it is currently connected to.
Note: A connection has to be previously established with the Connect API.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Restarts the pc-simulator stone.Target.Restart() Download(projectName, connectionString)Description:
Downloads the previous build to the currently connected target.
Notes:
The connection to the target, if open, must first be closed with the Disconnect API.
The solution must be opened with the Solution.Open API first. A build has to be performed with the Solution.Build API first.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project of the currently open (not the name of the solution) to be downloaded.
e.g. “pCOProject1” connectionString string The Connection string to the target.
e.g. “TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122” or “Serial,COM11,1152008N1,248” for serial. Example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") CreateWatch(VarToRead)Description:
Creates a Watch object to read from and write to application variables.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description variable string The name of the variable to watch (with namespaces if any) the same as watches view in STone IDE.
e.g. “MySetPoint”, “MainInstance.MyFunctionBlock.MySetPoint”. Returns:
Returns a tuple of a Watch object and a Result object.
Example:
ST example:
VAR_GLOBAL MyVar: INT := 1234; END_VAR PROGRAM Main MyVar := MyVar; END_PROGRAM IronPython example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (my_var, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MyVar") if result.IsSuccessful: # Read from variable MyVar (value, result) = my_var.ReadValue() print(value) # Output 1234 # Write to variable MyVar, set value 5678 my_var.WriteValue("5678") # Read from variable MyVar (value, result) = my_var.ReadValue() print(value) # Output 5678 StartStopDeviceRecover(comPort)Description:
Starts or Stops the device recover on the specified comPort.
Tip: It is advisable to put a delay between two calls of StartStopDeviceRecover API to allow the controller to be switched off and on again.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description comPort string The COM port of the controller.
e.g. “COM4”. Example:
# Starts DeviceRecover on COM11 stone.Target.StartStopDeviceRecover("COM11") # Stops DeviceRecover on COM11 stone.Target.StartStopDeviceRecover("COM11") ClearBinaries()Description:
Clears the currently downloaded application binaries from the target.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Stops the pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() stone.Target.ClearBinaries()

officialPages.title: Watch
officialPages.officialContent:
Watch class This class contains all the APIs to manage a watch, so it is possible to read from and write to values of a connected target.
To read and write values a valid target must be already connected with matching sources with an opened solution.
Watch is part of the Target class.
Target contains an array of all the watches created (see more in the “Target” page).
Watch class is also returned from the CreateWatch() API of Target class.
Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
ReadValue()Description:
Read the value of a variable from the connected target.
Returns:
Returns a tuple of a string (with variable value) and a Result object.
The string will be empty if no read could be performed.
Example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (set_point, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MySetPoint") # Read from variable MySetPoint (value, result) = set_point.ReadValue() # Stops pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() WriteValue(value)Description:
Write a value to a variable of the connected target.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description value string The value to be written.
e.g. “12”. Returns:
Returns a Result object.
Example:

officialPages.title: Task
officialPages.officialContent:
Task class This class contains all the APIs to get some information of the task present in the target, so it is possible to get the name, the status, the error message and the relative callstack, finally it can get and set if this is the active task.
Task is part of the Target class. Target contains an array of all the Tasks present in the Target (see more in the “Target” page) and a direct reference to the active Task.
The APIs works for both pc simulator and physical controller.
Fields Field Data type Description Name string Name of this task. Status string Status of this task. ErrorCode int If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the error code, otherwise 0. ErrorMessage string If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the error message, otherwise it is an empty string. Active bool “true” if this is the Active task, “false” otherwise. CallStack Array[string] If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the stack trace. The following is a non-exhaustive list of possible Status:
“Undefined” “Error” “OnCreation” “Stopped” “Running” “RunningStep” “RunningStepOver” “RunningStepOut” “Break” “Deleted” “Waiting” “Resumed” Example: Search for open libraries and close them.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Get the active task (activeTask, result) = stone.Target.ActiveTask # Print the name active task if(result.IsSuccessful): print(activeTask.Name) stone.Target.StopSimulator() Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
SetActive()Description:
Set this task as the active task.
Returns:
True if we change the Active task, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Get all task (tasks, result) = stone.Target.Tasks # Change the active task if(result.IsSuccessful): for task in tasks: if task.Name == "IEC_TaskName": task.SetActive() # Check if the active task is changed (activeTask, activeResult) = stone.Target.ActiveTask # Print the name of the new task if(activeResult.IsSuccessful): print(activeTask.Name) stone.Target.StopSimulator()

officialPages.title: Result
officialPages.officialContent:
Result class This class contains the information on the status of execution returned from some APIs, so it is possible to verify if the execution ended successfully and consult errors description if any.
Checking whether the execution of an API was successful can be done quickly by checking the value of the boolean field IsSuccessful of the Result class.
Result contains Errors, Warnings, Messages.
They are arrays of Note class.
Note class contains a string field called Description with more information of the execution of an API.
Fields Field Data type Description IsSuccessful bool True if API executed without errors, False otherwise. Errors Array[Note] List of all errors represented with Note class, if any. Warnings Array[Note] List of all warnings represented with Note class, if any. Messages Array[Note] List of all messages represented with Note class, if any. Example: Since Errors, Warnings and Messages are lists, you can cycle them with a for.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Build the solution result = stone.Solution.Build() # Print build errors, warnings and messages if build failed if not result.IsSuccessful: for error in result.Errors: print(error.Description) for warning in result.Warnings: print(warning.Description) for message in result.Messages: print(message.Description)

cliPages.title: Python Integration
cliPages.officialContent:
Base concepts STone provides a command line interface (SToneCLI.exe) to interact with some functionalities of the IDE, for example:
Build Automatic test Metadata generation Export workspace The CLI permits a Python integration using scripts.
The scripts can be usefull for continuous integration, continuous delivery and testing.
Following some snippet of Python scripts to call the CLI of STone using version >3.3
How to Here some simple steps to starting coding Python and calling “SToneCLI build”:
Using STone IDE create a project called “BaseProject2” in “C:\STone\Projects\” path Download and install Python version >3.3 Create file called “build.py” Open and edit the file using a text editor Paste the following code into the file: import subprocess import shlex def process_executor(exe: str, *args) -> int: command = '"' + exe + '"' + ' ' + ' '.join(args) print('Running command: ' + command) return subprocess.run(shlex.split(command)).returncode stone_cli = 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Carel\\STone\\SToneCLI.exe' process_executor(stone_cli, 'build', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"') Open a console Move to the folder containing the Python script Run the command: python.exe build.py Pay attention to SToneCLI.exe path and STone solution path.
It is possible to run and debug the script using IDE like Visual Studio Code or PyCharm.
In the next section will be explained the Python script.
Run executable The function “process_executor” runs an executable (as a subprocess) and returns the exit code.
import subprocess import shlex def process_executor(exe: str, *args) -> int: command = '"' + exe + '"' + ' ' + ' '.join(args) print('Running command: ' + command) return subprocess.run(shlex.split(command)).returncode Build To build a STone project use the follow command:
SToneCLI.exe build -s SOLUTION_FOLDER -p PROJECT_NAME -c CONFIGURATION_NAME Parameters Parameter Description -s Solution file path -p Project name -c Configuration name Example SToneCLI.exe build -s "C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone" -p BaseProject2 -c Debug Python Using Python:
process_executor(stone_cli, 'build', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"') Automatic test To run all the automatic test defined in a project:
SToneCLI.exe automatic-test -s SOLUTION_FOLDER -p PROJECT_NAME -c CONFIGURATION_NAME -n CONNECTION_STRING Parameters Parameter Description Solution file path -s Project name -p Configuration name -c Connection string to the target -n Example SToneCLI.exe automatic-test -s "C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone" -p BaseProject2 -c Debug -n TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122 Python Using Python:
process_executor(stone_cli, 'automatic-test', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"', '-n', '"TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122"') Unit tests To run all the unit test defined in a project see Integrates with CI/CD (DevOps)
Metadata generation STone creates metadata file after build process in the output folder.
The file contains all the information about the project, some of these are:

} The languages supported by the project grouped by interface Hardware string “HEOS” The hardware supported by the project UserInterfaces strings[] [“SevenSegments”, “pGD1”] The interface supported by the project IdeVersion string “1.3.1.0” The version of STone Libraries object {

} List of the libraries included in the projects and their version LibrariesCount number 30 The counter of the libraries imported by the application StandardLibraryCount number 11 The counter of the standard libraries imported by the application RetainUsageMemory number 2768 Memory used by retain variables (byte) RetainUsageMemoryPercentage number 4.0 Memory used by retain variables (percentage) RomUsageMemory number 451778 ROM memory used by project (byte) RomUsageMemoryPercentage number 43.0 ROM memory used by project (%) RamUsageMemory number 177666 RAM memory used by project (byte) RamUsageMemoryPercentage number 16.0 RAM memory used by project (%) NfcUsageMemory number 1264 NFC memory used by project (byte) NfcUsageMemoryPercentage number 79.0 NFC memory used by project (%) TestSuiteCount number 16 Number of Automatic Test Test suites TestCaseCount number 136 Number of Automatic Test Test cases TestStepCount number 2287 Number of Automatic Test Test steps Protocols strings[] [“Modbus - Client”, “Modbus - Server”] Protocols used by the project. cliPages.title: Integrates with CI/CD (DevOps)
cliPages.officialContent:
CI/CD is a set of practices and tools that enable the automation of building, testing, and deploying software changes.
STone IDE’s Unit Tests are designed with CI/CD (DevOps) integrations in mind, allowing seamless incorporation into the development and deployment pipeline.
When it comes to unit testing, CI/CD integration involves automating the execution of unit tests as part of the CI/CD process.
This ensures that the code changes made by developers do not introduce regressions or break existing functionality.
Integrating Unit Tests into the CI/CD pipeline provides immediate feedback on the status of tests, developers can catch issues early in the development process enabling them to quickly iterate and fix issues.
It promotes a culture of automated testing and helps ensure the overall stability and quality of the software being developed.
Unit Tests execution can be automated through the use of SToneCLI.
SToneCLI is a Command Line Interface (CLI) with, among other features, the unit-tests command to run unit tests and analyze code coverage.
It is possible to set a minimum required coverage percentage, when the total coverage is below the desired threshold the CLI execution will fail, alerting the developers.
It is also possible to generate log files in common format (JUnit, Cobertura) compatible with common CI/CD platforms.
Overall, the CI/CD integration of Unit Tests facilitates a smooth workflow by automating the execution of tests, ensuring adequate code coverage, and integrating testing into the larger development and deployment process.
SToneCLI Unit Tests commands Within SToneCLI it is possible to use the unit-tests command to run and optionally analyze code coverage.
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\CAREL\STone" SToneCLI.exe unit-tests -s "C:\Path\to\solution.stone" -p "ProjectName" -r "report.xml" -c "coverage.xml" -m "70" -n "TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122" --code-coverage Parameter Required / Optional Description -s Required The path to STone solution file. -p Required The name of the project to build and download. -r Optional Report file path. If specified, a Junit report file will be created in the desired path. --code-coverage Optional (Default: False) Enables: Analyze Code Coverage. -c Optional, must enable code coverage Code Coverage report file path. If specified, a Cobertura report file will be created in the desired path. -m Optional, must enable code coverage Minimum Code Coverage. If specified, if the total Code Coverage is less than the desired value the execution fails. --log-level Optional (Default: Normal) [ Verbose | Normal | Quiet ], Verbose: all information, Normal: normal information and errors, Quiet: only errors. -n Optional Connection string to the target SToneCLI exit codes for unit-tests command Exit Code Description 0 No errors (All Tests Passed). -1 Invalid STone license. -2 Solution path file not found. -3 Failed to load solution. -4 Project not found. -5 Project build fails. -6 Unit Tests build fails. -7 Unit Tests not found. -8 Connection fails. -9 Download fails. -10 Tests execution failed. -11 Unknown error. -12 Code Coverage less than minimum.

allMethods.name: SetActive()

allMethods.returns: True if we change the Active task, false otherwise.

examples.code:
# Open the stone solution
stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone")

# Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file
for project in stone.Solution.Projects:
if project.Name == "MyProjectName":
project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib")
project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs")

# Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build
stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName")
stone.Solution.Save()
stone.Solution.Build()

# Starts pc-simulator
stone.Target.StartSimulator()

# Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator
stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122")

# Get all task
(tasks, result) = stone.Target.Tasks

# Change the active task
if(result.IsSuccessful):
for task in tasks:
if task.Name == "IEC_TaskName":
task.SetActive()

# Check if the active task is changed
(activeTask, activeResult) = stone.Target.ActiveTask

# Print the name of the new task
if(activeResult.IsSuccessful):
print(activeTask.Name)

stone.Target.StopSimulator()

items.description:
Protocols.PeripheralInfo –

Members

Name
Description

PeripheralType
Peripheral identifier

FWRelease
FW Version: Major*100 + Minor

ProtocolCap
Bit 0: Message “r” (Carel protocol only)
Bit 1: crc error control (Carel protocol only)
Bit 2: accepts ‘U’, ‘S’, ‘B’ (Carel protocol only)
Bit 3: The device can switch between Carel and Modbus protocol (Carel and Modbus protocols)
Bit 4: accepts firmware download messages (Carel and Modbus protocols)
Bit 5: accepts EEPROM direct writing messages (Carel and Modbus protocol)
Bit 6: reserved for bootloader
Bit 7: the host of CAN bus board is a client of broadcast CAN bus mode (just for Idronic board)
Bit 8: Exception 5 (ACKNOWLEDGE) managed (Modbus protocol only)
Bit 15: At the end of PeripheralInfo message is added an extension of ProtocolCap

HWCode
Hardware code (input/output)

ExportIfaceCode
Code or version of variables’ database

ApplicationRelease
Application version

ApplicationCode
Application code

CustomerCode
Customer code

USMaxVar
Analog/Integer Max Var

BMaxVAr
Digital Max Var

ExtendedProtCap
This field is present in the PeripheralInfo message
if at least one of these things happens:
1) The bit 15 of ProtocolCap is set to 1;
2) It will be necessary to add other fields in queue, after the field ExtendedProtCap.
It is reserved for future extensions of ProtocolCap field.

Returns 0 in case of success, 1 otherwise
Synopsis USINT ClearSettings()
Examples USING System; USING System.UI; VAR_GLOBAL CONSTANT PAR1 : UDINT := 20; PAR2 : UDINT := 21; PAR3 : UDINT := 25; PAR4 : UDINT := 30; END_VAR VAR_GLOBAL bigData : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name : STRING := 'Device1'; password : STRING := 'Safe'; END_VAR PROGRAM main (*** Insert strategy here ***) VAR init : BOOL := TRUE; i : INT; tmpB : BYTE; tmpW : WORD; tmpDW : DWORD; bigData2 : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name2 : STRING; str : STRING;	END_VAR IF init THEN FOR i:= 0 TO 1499 BY 1 DO bigData[i] := TO_BYTE(i MOD 50); END_FOR; init := FALSE; END_IF; (* Sets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 *) SetSettingB(PAR1, 25); (* Gets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 and write this in tmpB *) GetSettingB(PAR1, tmpB); (* Sets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 *) SetSettingW(PAR2, 65000); (* Gets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 and write this in tmpW *) GetSettingW(PAR2, tmpW); (* Sets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 *) SetSettingDW(PAR3, 3000000000); (* Gets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 and write this in tmpDW *) GetSettingDW(PAR3, tmpDW); (* Sets the settings with offset PAR4 *) SetSetting(PAR4, bigData); (* Gets the settings with offset PAR4 and write this in bigData2 *) GetSetting(PAR4, bigData2); (* Sets the current machine name *) SetNameSetting(name); (* Gets the current machine name *) GetNameSetting(name2); (* Sets the current Password settings *) SetPasswordSetting(password); (* Gets the current Password settings *) GetPasswordSetting(str); (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM FUNCTION ManageKey : BOOL VAR_INPUT keyPressed, keyCounter : UINT; END_VAR IF keyPressed = KEY_ENTER THEN (* Clears all settings from internal retained memory *) ClearSettings(); END_IF; (*** Insert UI here ***) ManageKey:=TRUE; END_FUNCTION ClearSystemSettings() System.ClearSystemSettings – Clears the system settings from internal retained memory.
Pay attention that this function resets the device configuration
Returns 0 in case of success, 1 otherwise
Synopsis USINT ClearSystemSettings()
Examples USING System; USING System.UI; VAR_GLOBAL CONSTANT PAR1 : UDINT := 20; PAR2 : UDINT := 21; PAR3 : UDINT := 25; PAR4 : UDINT := 30; END_VAR VAR_GLOBAL bigData : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name : STRING := 'Device1'; password : STRING := 'Safe'; END_VAR PROGRAM main (*** Insert strategy here ***) VAR init : BOOL := TRUE; i : INT; tmpB : BYTE; tmpW : WORD; tmpDW : DWORD; bigData2 : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name2 : STRING; str : STRING;	END_VAR IF init THEN FOR i:= 0 TO 1499 BY 1 DO bigData[i] := TO_BYTE(i MOD 50); END_FOR; init := FALSE; END_IF; (* Sets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 *) SetSettingB(PAR1, 25); (* Gets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 and write this in tmpB *) GetSettingB(PAR1, tmpB); (* Sets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 *) SetSettingW(PAR2, 65000); (* Gets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 and write this in tmpW *) GetSettingW(PAR2, tmpW); (* Sets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 *) SetSettingDW(PAR3, 3000000000); (* Gets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 and write this in tmpDW *) GetSettingDW(PAR3, tmpDW); (* Sets the settings with offset PAR4 *) SetSetting(PAR4, bigData); (* Gets the settings with offset PAR4 and write this in bigData2 *) GetSetting(PAR4, bigData2); (* Sets the current machine name *) SetNameSetting(name); (* Gets the current machine name *) GetNameSetting(name2); (* Sets the current Password settings *) SetPasswordSetting(password); (* Gets the current Password settings *) GetPasswordSetting(str); (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM FUNCTION ManageKey : BOOL VAR_INPUT keyPressed, keyCounter : UINT; END_VAR IF keyPressed = KEY_ENTER THEN (* Clears all settings from internal retained memory *) ClearSettings(); END_IF; (*** Insert UI here ***) ManageKey:=TRUE; END_FUNCTION CreateDynamicEvent() System.CreateDynamicEvent – Creates a new dynamic event.
Returns dynamic event mask if the event was created successfully; error code otherwise.
Synopsis DWORD CreateDynamicEvent()
Examples USING System; PROGRAM Main VAR taskID : UINT; eventID : DWORD; customData : UDINT; END_VAR //Create dynamic event eventID := CreateDynamicEvent(); //Get event driven task ID taskID := GetTaskId(EventTask); //Subscribe event on an event driven task SubscribeEvent(taskID, eventID); //Fire user event on EventTask task with a 10ms delay SignalDynamicEvent(customData, 10, eventID); //Unsubscribe dynamic event from event driven task EventTask UnsubscribeEvent(taskID, eventID); //Free dynamic event FreeDynamicEvent(eventID); END_PROGRAM PROGRAM EventProgram VAR_TEMP event : Event; eventsCount : INT; error : INT; END_VAR //Get current event task pending events count eventsCount := GetEventsCount(); IF eventsCount = 1 THEN //Get current event error := GetCurrentEvent(event); //Manage event ELSIF eventsCount > 1 THEN //While there are pending events WHILE GetEventsCount() > 0 DO //Get first not managed event of the pending list error := GetNextEvent(event); IF error = DINT_TO_INT(ERR_OK) THEN //Manage event ELSE //Manage event error END_IF; END_WHILE; END_IF; END_PROGRAM CONFIGURATION Configuration1 RESOURCE Resource1 ON DEMOTARGET TASK MainTask (INTERVAL:=t#300ms, PRIORITY:=3); PROGRAM MainInstance WITH MainTask : Main; TASK EventTask (EVENT:=DYNAMIC_EVENT); PROGRAM EventInstance WITH EventTask : EventProgram; END_RESOURCE END_CONFIGURATION DataType System.DataType – List of DataType

The ‘unit’ input variable is the number of the peripheral. Its value is ‘0’

Returns LIB_FS_OK if the configuration will be applied,
LIB_FS_ERR_VOLUME_ACCESS otherwise.

If XIN1 exceeds XIN2 by the value specified by input EPS, the output Q is TRUE.
The output Q remains TRUE until the input XIN1 is less than the value XIN2, by the value of EPS.
The value of Q then become FALSE.

items.description:
System.Math.RATIO_MONITOR – Checks that one process value PV1 is always a given ratio (defined by input RATIO)
of a second process value PV2.
If the error between the values of PV1 and PV2, as required to mantain the ratio,
goes outside the given TOLERANCE, an alarm timer is started.
If the error exists for longer than the time specified by TIMON, the ALARM output is set on.

Timer on delay supplies the input value IN at Q with a time delay when
a rising edge is detected at IN.
If input IN is only ‘1’ for a short pulse(shorter than PT),
the timer is not started for this edge.

Returns TRUE if desidered mode was set, returns FALSE otherwise.
Synopsis BOOL SetUsbHostMode(System.USB.UsbHostMode) [Input] System.USB.UsbHostMode mode;
+---------------------------+| System.USB.SetUsbHostMode || |System.USB.UsbHostMode-| mode |+---------------------------+Parameters Name Type Description mode System.USB.UsbHostMode - UsbDeviceMode System.USB.UsbDeviceMode – Usb device mode Members Name Description CdcMode Communication Device Class (CDC) mode: the USB port becomes a virtual serial port. MtpMode Media Transfer Protocol (MTP) mode: allows to transfer files to and from a Personal Computer. NoneMode USB device disabled Examples (* This example shows how to check the status of the connection with a USB device and how to set and get its mode, by choosing one of the following options: - CDC = Communication Device Class (virtual serial port) - MTP = Media Transfer Protocol (file transfer with a personal computer) - disabled *) USING System.UI; USING System.USB; VAR_GLOBAL mode : System.USB.UsbDeviceMode := UsbDeviceMode#NoneMode; device_ready : BOOL; error : BOOL := FALSE; END_VAR PROGRAM Main VAR current_mode : System.USB.UsbDeviceMode := UsbDeviceMode#NoneMode; result : BOOL; first_run : BOOL := TRUE; END_VAR; IF first_run THEN first_run := FALSE; (* Read the configured mode from the device *) System.USB.GetUsbDeviceMode(mode); END_IF; device_ready := System.USB.IsUsbDeviceReady(); (* The error, if present, must be manually removed from the UI *) IF error = FALSE THEN IF current_mode <> mode THEN current_mode := mode; (* Set the current mode, according to the UI *) result := System.USB.SetUsbDeviceMode(mode); IF result = FALSE THEN error := TRUE; ELSE error := FALSE; END_IF; END_IF; END_IF; (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM UsbHostMode System.USB.UsbHostMode – Usb host mode Members Name Description NoneMode USB host disabled MsdMode Mass Storage Device (MSD) mode: allows to transfer files to and from a USB pen drive. Examples (* This example shows how to implement the communication with a pen drive by setting the proper mode and checking if the drive is ready. Furthermore it shows how to write a file on the drive. *) USING System; USING System.UI; USING System.USB; USING System.FileSystem; USING System.Timer; VAR_GLOBAL info : System.SystemInfo; mode : System.USB.UsbHostMode := UsbHostMode#NoneMode; error : DINT(-20..9) := 0; write_file : USINT := 0; host_ready : BOOL; dateTime : System.Timer.DateTime; enableLabel : BOOL; END_VAR PROGRAM Main VAR current_mode : System.USB.UsbHostMode := UsbHostMode#NoneMode; result : BOOL; first_run : BOOL := TRUE; partition : System.FileSystem.Enums.PartitionType := System.FileSystem.Enums.PartitionType#PenDrive; filepath : STRING := 'test.txt'; openmode : System.FileSystem.Enums.FS_OpenMode := System.FileSystem.Enums.FS_OpenMode#OPEN_CREAT; file_id : DINT; written_bytes : DINT; text : STRING := 'test'; END_VAR; IF first_run THEN first_run := FALSE; (* Read the configured mode from the device *) System.USB.GetUsbHostMode(mode); END_IF; host_ready := System.USB.IsUsbHostReady(); System.Timer.GetTime(dateTime); IF dateTime.Second MOD 2 = 0 THEN enableLabel := TRUE; ELSE enableLabel := FALSE; END_IF; (* The error, if present, must be manually removed from the UI *) IF error = 0 THEN IF current_mode <> mode THEN current_mode := mode; (* Set the current mode, according to the UI *) result := System.USB.SetUsbHostMode(mode); IF result = FALSE THEN error := -1; ELSE error := 0; END_IF; END_IF; (* Check for a push of the PRG key to save a file on the pen drive *) IF mode = UsbHostMode#MsdMode THEN IF write_file = 1 THEN file_id := System.FileSystem.FileOpen(partition, filepath, openmode); IF file_id >= 0 THEN write_file := 2; ELSE write_file := 3; error := file_id; END_IF; ELSIF write_file = 2 THEN write_file := 3; written_bytes := System.FileSystem.FileWrite(file_id, text); IF written_bytes < 0 THEN error := written_bytes; ELSE error := 0; END_IF; ELSIF write_file = 3 THEN System.FileSystem.FileClose(file_id); END_IF; END_IF; END_IF; (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM FUNCTION set_write_file write_file := 1; error := 0; END_FUNCTION

allItems.name: PeripheralInfo
allItems.description:
Protocols.PeripheralInfo –

Members

Name
Description

PeripheralType
Peripheral identifier

FWRelease
FW Version: Major*100 + Minor

ProtocolCap
Bit 0: Message “r” (Carel protocol only)
Bit 1: crc error control (Carel protocol only)
Bit 2: accepts ‘U’, ‘S’, ‘B’ (Carel protocol only)
Bit 3: The device can switch between Carel and Modbus protocol (Carel and Modbus protocols)
Bit 4: accepts firmware download messages (Carel and Modbus protocols)
Bit 5: accepts EEPROM direct writing messages (Carel and Modbus protocol)
Bit 6: reserved for bootloader
Bit 7: the host of CAN bus board is a client of broadcast CAN bus mode (just for Idronic board)
Bit 8: Exception 5 (ACKNOWLEDGE) managed (Modbus protocol only)
Bit 15: At the end of PeripheralInfo message is added an extension of ProtocolCap

HWCode
Hardware code (input/output)

ExportIfaceCode
Code or version of variables’ database

ApplicationRelease
Application version

ApplicationCode
Application code

CustomerCode
Customer code

USMaxVar
Analog/Integer Max Var

BMaxVAr
Digital Max Var

ExtendedProtCap
This field is present in the PeripheralInfo message
if at least one of these things happens:
1) The bit 15 of ProtocolCap is set to 1;
2) It will be necessary to add other fields in queue, after the field ExtendedProtCap.
It is reserved for future extensions of ProtocolCap field.

allItems.name: HYSTERESIS
allItems.description:
System.Math.HYSTERESIS – Provides a hysteresis boolean output driven by the difference of two REAL inputs XIN1 and XIN2.
If XIN1 exceeds XIN2 by the value specified by input EPS, the output Q is TRUE.
The output Q remains TRUE until the input XIN1 is less than the value XIN2, by the value of EPS.
The value of Q then become FALSE.

allItems.name: INTEGRAL
allItems.description:
System.Math.INTEGRAL – Integrates the value of input XIN over time.
The integration can be reset to a preset value X0 by setting the reset input R1 to true.
The CYCLE time defines the time between function block executions.
The output XOUT is integrated while the RUN input is true; otherwise the integration value is held.
The Q output is true while the integral is not being reset.

allItems.name: RATIO_MONITOR
allItems.description:
System.Math.RATIO_MONITOR – Checks that one process value PV1 is always a given ratio (defined by input RATIO)
of a second process value PV2.
If the error between the values of PV1 and PV2, as required to mantain the ratio,
goes outside the given TOLERANCE, an alarm timer is started.
If the error exists for longer than the time specified by TIMON, the ALARM output is set on.
