help.title: About
help.officialContent:
About STone IDE provides a set of APIs designed to allow users to automate common tasks such as building projects, updating libraries, and downloading to a target, programmatically.
In this documentation, detailed information are provided about these APIs, including the parameters they accept, their return values and sample code snippets to demonstrate their usage.
These APIs can be used within a Python script, which is then executed by SToneCLI.exe via the command:
SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f C:/Path/to/script/example.py Note:
The Python runtime is IronPython, which is a .NET implementation of the Python programming language.
This differs from the standard CPython runtime, but users do not need to install anything other than STone IDE to use these APIs.
The Python version supported is 3.4 (Documentation)
To add external modules append them to sys.path
APIs Overview Below is an overview of the APIs in UML diagram:
APIs usually have a return boolean value, useful to check if the call was successful.
It is recommended to read the documentation in the following order:
stone Solution Project Target Watch Task Example First create a python script which uses the STone APIs.
Python script example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (set_point, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MySetPoint") # Read from variable MySetPoint (value, result) = set_point.ReadValue() print(value) # Stops pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() Then execute it with SToneCLI:
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\CAREL\STone" SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f C:/Path/to/script/example.py Command options iron-python command accepts the following options:
-f, --python-file The path to the python script file to be executed, required. -a, --script-args The arguments to be passed to the python script, optional.
First argument is always the given script path. Example of arguments usage: IronPython script:
import sys print(sys.argv) CLI call:
SToneCLI.exe iron-python -f .\script.py -a first second "third argument" Output:
['.\\script.py', 'first', 'second', 'third argument'] SToneCLI exit codes for iron-python command Exit Code Description 0 No errors from python runtime (e.g. No exceptions). -1 Invalid STone license. -2 Python file not found. -3 Python exception.

help.title: About
help.officialContent:
STone IDE offers a range of features for writing, running, and debugging Unit Tests, enhancing the software development process.
Unit Tests are a specific type of white box testing method.
They involve testing the smallest functional units of a software system, such as POUs (FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK, CLASS, METHOD, etc.), to ensure their proper functioning.
By decomposing the software’s functionality into discrete and testable behaviors, these units can be tested individually and in isolation.
Structured Text code is used to write Unit Tests in STone IDE, which can then be executed through the Unit Tests Explorer. This approach enables automated, repeatable, and continuous testing.
STone IDE’s Unit Tests are designed with CI/CD (DevOps) integrations in mind, allowing seamless incorporation into the development and deployment pipeline.
Furthermore, STone IDE’s Unit Tests offer the capability to analyze Code Coverage.
Code Coverage is an objective measure that quantifies the extent to which the tests cover the application code.
By leveraging STone IDE’s Unit Testing capabilities, developers can enhance their software development workflow, ensuring the reliability and quality of their codebase.
Write Unit Tests Write Unit Tests with all the power of Structured Text.
Run them with Unit Tests Explorer Execute and see the results in the Unit Tests Explorer.
Analyze Code Coverage See how much of your code is covered by Unit Tests.
Integrates with CI/CD Enables the DevOps workflow and automate test execution.

help.title: STone
help.officialContent:
File menu New project creates a new project; Close closes the current opened file; Close solution closes the current solution; Save active editor saves the current opened file; Save solution saves all files and configurations of the current active solution; Exit exits the program. File ➝ Open menu Open ➝ Solution opens an existing solution; Open ➝ File opens an existing file into the editor. File ➝ Recent solutions menu Recent solutions sub-menu displays a list of the most recent solutions opened with STone. This list is also available into the welcome page.
View menu Welcome page opens Welcome page docking window; Solution Explorer opens Solution Explorer docking window; Global variables opens Variable View for global variables docking window. Symbols opens Symbols docking window; Errors opens Errors docking window; Output opens Output docking window; Memory Occupation opens Memory Occupation docking window; Properties opens Properties docking window; Find and replace opens Find and replace docking window; Find results 1 opens Find results 1 docking window; Find results 2 opens Find results 2 docking window; Find symbols results opens Find symbols results docking window; Find translation references opens Find translation references docking window; Bookmarks opens Bookmarks docking window; Targets opens Targets docking window; Target Log opens Target Log docking window; Task monitor opens Task monitor docking window; System Errors opens System Errors docking window; IO Hardware Simulator opens IO Hardware Simulator docking window; Commissioning opens Commissioning docking window; Reset windows layout Reset windows layout to default setting. View ➝ ToolBars menu LoadSave shows solution load and save commands in main toolbar; Undo Redo shows Undo Redo commands in main toolbar; Cut Copy Paste shows Cut Copy Paste commands in main toolbar; Prev Next shows Previous Next position commands in main toolbar; View shows dock windows opening commands in main toolbar; Build shows all Build related commands in main toolbar; Simulator shows all Simulator related commands in main toolbar; Debug shows all Debug related commands in main toolbar; Text editor shows all Text editor related commands in main toolbar; Build menu Full build performs a complete build; Build for online changes performs a build of the POUs that contains changes; Batch build opens Batch build window, that could be used to perform multiple builds with different configurations with one click; Config manager opens Solution configuration manager window, that could be used to set different build configurations. Debug menu Start task starts the selected task, if it is not running; Break task breaks the selected task, if it is running; Stop task stops the selected task, if it is not stopped; Step into task steps into the current statement; Step over task steps over the current statement; Step out task steps out the current statement; Go to cursor go to the cursor focused statement; Set next statement set the next executed statement. Debug ➝ Windows menu Call stack opens Call stack window; Breakpoints opens Breakpoints window; Profiling opens Profiling window; Code coverage opens Code coverage window; Watch 1 opens the first Watch window; Watch 2 opens the second Watch window. Chart 1 opens the first Chart window; Chart 2 opens the second Chart window. Memory 1 opens the first Memory window; Memory 2 opens the second Memory window. Test menu Unit Tests Explorer opens the Unit Tests Explorer window; Code Coverage Results opens the Code Coverage Results window; Tools menu Start simulator starts the simulator if it is not running, stops it otherwise ( Stop simulator is displayed); Erase simulator binaries deletes all simulator binaries, in case of problem; Target System Update (Package) opens a Target System Update window to create a binary package for upgrade device Firmware; Device recover opens a Device Recover window to force the default application sending a break the serial 0; Digital Signature opens a Digital Signature window to create a digital signature for a device; Plugin Manager opens a Plugin Manager window to check or install plugin for Stone. Options shows Options window, where you can (first tab): change the Language change the Font type change the Font size change the Theme on the second tab you can change simulation setting: change the WebServer TCP-IP port change connection port for TCP-IP connection (PC side) map the device serial port on the PC port for the simulation set if the simulator must be stopped when STone is closed set if the simulator should stop on every error (even when STone is not connected to the simulator) set if the simulator should stop on subrange error (even when STone is not connected to the simulator) change the value of Time multiplier License opens a License Manager window to manage license for Stone. Tools ➝ Plugin Manager Install Plugin Tab** List all the install plugins.
Install new plugin by clicking + icon.
Tools ➝ License License Activation The usual first activation will require filling out a form with the serial number (and other data) that will proceed with STone calling CLiM.
If the PC is offline, it corresponds to the old activation process.The user will send the HW ID to CST, and then receive a .jlic license file to install.
For older installations prior that already have a license file, here the user will be prompted to fill in some location info and then a serial number will be generated and associated with the already existing license by CLiM.
License Update If a license is installed, to update to manually add another serial number meant to enable some more features (e.g. passing from STone “basic” to “pro”) in Tools > License.
License Expired If a feature of license expired or the PC is offline for more than 30 days,a warning message will appear and the below listed functionalities will be disabled:
The build process the build process will be disabled Digital Signature the releated menu item will be hidden Automatic Test the inside functionalities will be forbidden and unable to add new Automatic Test Regression Test the inside functionalities will be forbidden and unable to add new Regression Test Unit Tests the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Code Coverage the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Memory Watch the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Profiling the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Target Log the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Watches Chart the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Hardware Simulator the inside functionalities will be forbidden and the releated menu item will be hidden Check the license and contact support if warning message appears.
Target contextual menu (Disconnected target) Connect connects STone with the selected target if it is set as active target, and it is not connected - if not, replacing it there is the entry Set as active target. If the target is connected, Disconnect is shown; Start all tasks starts all the stopped tasks, if any; Stop all tasks stops all the running tasks, if any; Restart application restarts the application that is into the target; Download application changes performs an application download to the target, downloading only the POUs that results modified from the application running into the target.
Is possible to perform this functionality only if the target is not running a modified POU; Full download performs a download of the entire application, erasing the one into the target; Full download default application performs a download of the default application, erasing the one into the target; Update System allows to update the Operating system, the Bootloader, or both at the same time; Retrieve Application allows to upload from the target the running’s application (binary file); Snapshot allows to upload from the target the last one snapshot taken, if exists; Logs allows to upload from the target the logs, if exists; Signature info allows to upload from the target the signature information, if exists; Default connection info allows to upload from the target the default connection information, if exists; Production info allows to upload from the target the production information, if exists; Security allows to: Change Binary Password: this password is used to protect the binary application download; Change Connection Password: this password is used to protect the IDE connection; Rename target renames the selected target (only into targets list); Remove target removes the selected target from targets list, if it is not the active target; Properties shows the Properties window, where is possible to say some information and to set the connection type and its parameters. The Fire! and Hot Reload buttons Fire! button is a button that allows to save some steps. Fire! button builds the current solution, connects to the current active target if it is not connected (starts the simulator if the current active target is it, and if it is not running), and performs a Full download operation.
The Hot Reload button (near Fire! Button) builds and download to the active target only the POUs that contains changes.
Target Menu ➝ Update System Update OS and bootloader tab Choose one or both the .bin files to download into the target.
If the files are valid, the Update System button will appear.
Install the new firmware by clicking Update System button.
Follow the instructions that will appear on the screen.
Edit project It is possible to open “project editor” tab in the contextual menu of the project in solution explorer.
General Tab In “general” tab there are the following information:
Name: the name of the project
File name: the absolute path to the project file
Variable View array/structure visible elements: changing the number you can set the number of visible elements for array and structures in the variable view. Decreasing this value can improve variable loading performance for projects that contain many nested variables. Value range is: 10 ~ 100, default value is 30. Digital signature application certificate: path of certificate to sign the application
Generate metadata file: enable or disable the generation of the file which collect the properties of the project.
Some properties are:
Project version Project name Solution name Languages: the languages supported by the project Memories usage: ROM/RAM/NFC/Retain memory used by project in byte and percentage. Global variables: list of defined and compiled variables in the project. Symbols: list of defined and compiled symbols in the project. The file will be created in the output folder.
For for information about this functionality, see the section in Python Integration page.

help.title: Libraries in STone
help.officialContent:
In STone IDE, libraries are pre-written code modules that provide reusable functionality.
They significantly streamline the development process, saving time and effort, and ensuring code reliability and consistency for more efficient software development.
They can be created and shared as a convenient “.stlib” file.
Creating a new library Right click on a symbol in your code Select Export To Library Or Right click on project inside solution explorer view Select Export To Library Then Select any symbol you wish to add to new library Any dependent symbol is automatically selected Use the text box to search specific symbols Right click on any symbol allows to select or unselect all items Press Ok when done or Cancel to abort operation Finally Select the library name or use the proposed one Choose the destination directory or use the proposed one Select the initial version (usually v.0.1.0) Optionally se the password to open it (can be changed after anyway) Press Ok when done or Cancel to abort operation Managing Library Packages Right click on Dependencies > Libs node allows to add, manage and update libraries. More on the Manage Libraries page. Right click on a Library Package allows to directly manage it: Double left click on a Library Package allows to open it A Library Package already opened in a Library Project cannot be deleted. Library Package Properties: File: File system Generic information Name: File name of Library package Full Path: path in file system where Library package is located Library Info: contains information about library UID: Project ID is generated only when Library is created and identify a Library regardless the Name, Version or sources Name: Internal Library Name. Reflect the Library Namespace Description: short description of what Library can do Author: Ownership information Vendor: Ownership information Version: Library Version. Reflect the Library Namespace Source CRC: CRC for source code. Project CRC: CRC for project. Samples: Reflect the presence of embedded sample projects explaining how to use the Library. Help: Reflect the presence of embedded help about Library. Library Security: contains information about Library security Protection: If Master Password was set is ‘Locked’ otherwise ‘Free’ Signature: If Library is signed by a manufacturer here is the its name Access: Access level could be ‘Read Only’ or ‘Full’. A Read Only Library cannot be saved back to its referred Library Package Library Projects Opened Library will be added to the Solution as Library Project The Library Project name contains, enclosed in brackets, a reference to the project from which was opened (eg. MyLib_v.0.1.0 [MyApp]) Library Project source is viewable and editable (unless protection has been set for specific files) Library Project source is included in searches (by text or by reference) Library Project debug is enabled (breakpoint and watches) Managing Library Project Library Project is like application project with some more options Set Version: changes or set Library Project Version. Save changes in referred library: save changes of Library Project back to referred Library Package. Version must be different. Save changes in other library: save changes of Library Project in a new Library Package (will be created a new Library ID) Set/Change Master Password: set/change Master Password to protect it against unauthorized opening, the length of password is 16. Library Projects Security Library Project can be protected with Master Password.
Library protected with Master Password will ask for password during Library Package opening. Library Project file can be protected with File Level Password.
File protected with File Level Password will ask for password during first file opening. !! IMPORTANT !! File just protected will be encrypted only when saved in a Library Package File in the project will remain unprotected until Project is closed.
Next time Library Package will be opened the file will be extracted encrypted.
File level Password is requested only one time during Library Project life. So, once opened with the correct password a protected file will be decrypted and will stay in that way until Project is closed.
Library Project Properties: Library: contains Library specific information UID: Library ID is generated only when Library is created and identify a Library regardless the Name, Version or sources Name: Internal Library Name. Reflect the Library Namespace Version: Library Version. Reflect the Library Namespace Description: short description of what Library can do Project: contains general project information Name: Project name with information about referred project Full path: The path in the file system where Project is located. For Library Projects the path points to a temporary directory like [..]\ProjProject1[321b8472-804d-4e8e-972b-13493f85f00a\Test.stprj UID: Project ID is generated when project is opened. It is used only by Application Projects Type: Project Type (Application or Library) Author: Ownership information Vendor: Ownership information Security: contains information about Library security Protection: If Master Password was set is ‘Locked’ otherwise ‘Free’ Signature: If Library is signed by a manufacturer here is the its name Access: Access level could be ‘Read Only’ or ‘Full’. A Read Only Library cannot be saved back to its referred Library Package Nested Libraries Library Project can contains Library Packages and so on recursively Library Project depending on other project cannot be removed. Library namespaces: Libraries are enclosed in specific namespace Libs.LibraryName_version. To access to the last version Library is possible to use the short format Libs.LibraryName Two or more Libraries with different versions (but same Project ID) can coexist. Use the Last Version feature and standard namespace with version to choose which use. Debug: Library Packages can be compiled but cannot be debugged. Library Projects sources can be viewed and edited. Breakpoints can be placed in Library Projects. Library Packages can’t. Step Into command jumps inside a Library Projects if needed. Library Packages can’t. Watch for Library Projects internal variables shows the values. Library Packages can’t. Library Projects behavior is the same of Application Project ones !! IMPORTANT !! Library Projects can be opened and closed (with some limitations) at any moment. But for enable the Debug features of a just opened Library Project a build must be performed even if no changes was made in the sources.

help.title: Modbus and CAREL Server
help.officialContent:
Base concepts - - Supervisor It represents both the transmission channel and the protocol running over the channel from the point-of-view of a server. It contains the informations about the channel (Serial or TcpIp) and about the protocol (Modbus or Carel). It publishes a list of variables over the protocol. It is unaware of the presence of a client. Configurator It represents the environment in which you configure server protocols. It collects all the configurations of servers in the .stsp file. Configuration It represents an instance of supervisor. Task Each protocol configuration (supervisor) will run asynchronously in a specific event-driven task. Server configurator The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the server configurations.
1 - List of the configurations 2 - List of the variables published by the focused configuration 3 - Publish-variable columns within the “Global Variables” tab 4 - Property grid 1. List of the configurations It shows the list of the server configurations belonging to the current project.
The Modbus configurations have the icon: The Carel configurations have the icon: Near by the name there are rapid informations about the configuration:
For serial supervisors, in brackets, the respective COM port is displayed. For TcpIp supervisors, in brackets, the respective protocol (TCP or UDP) and port are displayed. On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a server configuration Delete the focused server configuration Import an existing server configuration Export the focused server configuration Define the task priority (Advanced) Display the properties of the focused server configuration on the property grid 2. List of the variables published by the focused configuration This view collects the informations about the variables published by a configuration.
It collects the internal informations (name and type) about the specific variable.
It is possible to choose index, protocol-kind and size in terms of occupation of registers.
On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Delete the selected variables Sort the variables by type (registers, coils) and index Choose the Zone 3. Publish-variable columns within the “Global Variables” tab Inside the “Global Variables” tab, pressing the button, you access the publish-variable columns.
In each column, the ticked variables are published in the respective configuration.
Notes about server memory for declared variables The protocol engine (Modbus or Carel) needs an internal memory where to store a copy of the protocol data. This memory is defined for each kind (e.g. Analog for CAREL protocol, HoldingRegister for Modbus) starting from the lowest index to the highest index defined.
The Modbus standard allows only contiguous registers definition.
Example:
In a Modbus Server, if a Holding Register is defined at index 5 and another one is defined at index 50, the memory for 46 registers is allocated.
4. Property grid It shows the main properties of the configuration.
Different properties are shown according to the type of configuration (Serial or TcpIp).
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current server configuration.
How to configure a server In order to configure a server protocol you need to:
Add the server protocol configurator Create a server configuration Publish the variables Add the server protocol configurator After creating a STone project, it is possible to add a server configurator.
In the “Solution explorer” tab, right-click on the name of the project and choose Add => Add server protocols configurator.
In the solution will be created the file “ServerProtocols.stsp” and the editor will open.
Create a server configuration Open the server protocols configurator.
Click the “Add configuration” button. The wizard will open.
Follow the instructions and configure with the proper settings.
Remember to copy-and-paste in the main program the block of code in the last page of the wizard in order to make the just-created protocol task run.
It is possible to edit the property of a configuration using the property grid.
The properties of a server configuration, shown in property grid too, are: Name is the configuration’s name Protocol is the configuration’s protocol (Read Only) Bits are the used serial bits (only for serial configurations) IDE Mode is the serial port IDE access (only for serial configurations) Parity is the used serial parity (only for serial configurations) Speed is the serial baudrate (only for serial configurations) Stop Bits Bits are the used serial stop bits (only for serial configurations) Check FORCE enable check to force the server to receive a FORCE command before starting the communication; when offline (timeout expired) the controller wont respond until a FORCE is sent (only for CAREL serial configurations) Enable MOPL Enables the MOPL (Modbus over pLAN) if the supervisor line is configured to run on the Serial0 and the pLan protocol is running (only for Modbus Server configurations). Check Modbus over pLAN section for further details Ident is the server address Port is the communication serial port or TcpIp port (respectively for serial and TcpIp configurations) Protocol is the TcpIp protocol (only for TcpIp configurations) Timeout is the timeout to detect when the client becomes offline (only for serial configurations) Publish the variables Declare the variables to publish.
In the “Global variables” tab, click the button. The publish-variable columns will show up.
Tick the respective check-box in order to publish the variable.
The ticked variable will appear in the list of variables of the corresponding configuration.
It is possible to edit the property of a variable using the variables table.
The properties of a published variable, shown in the table, are: Name is the name of the variable (Read Only) Data Type is the type of the variable (Read Only) Variable Kind is the kind of the variable from the point-of-view of the protocol Variable Index is the starting index where the variable is published (0-based for Modbus, 1-based for Carel) Size is the number of registers (or coils) where the value of the variable is published Properties of the Supervisor Instance Since the supervisor is an instance of an object, a number of properties and methods are available.
The properties and methods of an instance of a server configuration are: The field SerialSettings collects the connection settings (only for serial configurations) (See Advanced) The field TCPSettings collects the connection settings (only for TcpIp configurations) (See Advanced) The field Info collects additional informations (see Advanced) The method Init initializes the server according to the settings defined in the property grid and starts the protocol The method Start starts the server operations The method Stop stops the server operations The method IsRunning returns true if the server operations are running The method Read reads the data from the protocol The method Write writes the data onto the protocol The method GetIdent returns the current server ident The method ChangeIdent sets the argument as the new current server ident The method ChangeSettings applies the current connection settings The method GetID is the internal ID of the configuration Advanced The fields of the SerialSettings struct are: Channel is the communication serial port Bits are the used serial bits Parity is the used serial parity Stops are the used serial stop bits Speed is the serial baudrate Mode is the serial port IDE access HWMode is the physical realization of the line (RS-485, RS-232) MaskEvent is the mask for the dynamic event associated with the protocol task The fields of the TcpSettings struct are: port is the communication tcp port proto is the protocol used over the ethernet (TCP or UDP) client is the IP address of the client (as an UDINT) mode is the tcp mpde (Server, Client or Test) EventMask is the mask for the dynamic event associated with the protocol task The fields of the Info struct are: Online tells the connection status of the server ExecutionTime is the time that the server took to process and reply to the last request PollInterval is the time passed between the last poll and the current one PollsCount is the number of requests that a server processed since it is running Timeout is the maximum time that can pass since the last processed request Zone is the UoM zone of the server ReportServerID sets the answer to a ReportServerId request (Modbus only) EnableMOPL Enables the MOPL (Modbus over pLAN) if the supervisor line is configured to run on the Serial0 and the pLan protocol is running (Modbus server only) Modbus over pLan MOPL (Modbus over pLan) is used to allow Modbus communication between devices connected in a running pLAN network (e.g. to connect a device to a pGDX). In order to enable MOPL:
The Enable MOPL flag in the server configuration properties or the Server.Info.EnableMOPL flag in ST code must be set to true before Start method is called Serial port must be the Serial0 pLan must be running (by default, pLan protocol is always running on Serial0) pLan network starts after the first call of SendVirtualKey method. In this case init method is called 2 times:
Note: this feature will work only for devices that supports pLan.

help.title: Write a Unit Test
help.officialContent:
Unit Tests consist of Test Suites and Test Cases.
A Test Suite contains one or more Test Cases.
A Test Case contains the code of the test to be executed.
A Test Suite is a CLASS, while a Test Case is a METHOD of the class marked with the metadata “{METADATA UNIT_TEST}”:
It is not necessary to know classes and methods to write unit tests.
There are code snippets to help writing Unit Tests, just start typing “test” or use the shortcut “CTRL + I” to select between Test Suite and Test Case snippets.
Variables (and instances of FUNCTION_BLOCK and CLASS) can be declared inside the Test Case (METHOD) that can then be used within the test.
In the body of the Test Case (METHOD) code for the test can be written.
Conditions can be checked with the Assert function of the System namespace.
The Assert function helps validate that certain conditions or expectations are true, otherwise the test will fail.
A Test Case can contain multiple Assert functions.
A Test Case is considered passed if no Assert functions failed and there where no runtime exceptions (Array out of bound, etc…).
A documentation for the Test Suites and Test Cases can be written above them that will be also displayed in the Test Info View of the Unit Test Explorer.
Setup and Teardown It is possible to write optional Setup and/or Teardown methods.
These methods are executed before and after each test case, respectively.
They help eliminate redundant code when multiple tests require the same initialization and cleanup steps.
Setup is called before each Test Case of the Test Suite in which they are defined.
Teardown, if defined, will be executed after each Test Case of the Test Suite in which they are defined.
Consequently, the execution order is as follows:
Setup Test Case Teardown Setup method is marked with the metadata “{METADATA TEST_SETUP}”
Teardown method is marked with the metadata “{METADATA TEST_TEARDOWN}”
There are code snippets to help writing Setup and Teardown, just start typing “setup”/“teardown” or use the shortcut “CTRL + I” inside a Test Suite.
If the Setup method encounters an exception during test execution, the current test will be considered failed, and the Test Case itself will not be executed.
Instead, the Teardown method will be called.
Furthermore, the Teardown method will be invoked whenever a Test Case fails due to an assertion error.
Test Project It is possible to optionally create a�Test Project to separate test code from application code.
Add it to the solution by “Right click on solution > New project > Select test project”.
A Test Project needs to reference other core projects by �Right click on test project > Add > Add Dependency Project�.
Core projects are projects created starting from the “Empty Project” template containing only POUs logic code (No UI, Protocols, Resources, etc…).
To be able to run tests defined inside a test project, first set it as the current active project ("Right click on test project > Set as active project").
How are Unit Tests executed Unit Tests are run in isolation.
STone IDE will generate a temporary configuration and program to call each test and verify the results.
While Unit Tests are running the Main task, UI task, Protocol task, etc… would not run and interfere with the test execution.
When compiling Unit Tests, STone will emit the “UNIT_TESTS_ARE_RUNNING” preprocessor definition.
Unit Tests are run by default on the active target (the speed at which Unit Tests are executed depends on the target; to achieve a higher execution speed, it is recommended to run them on the PC-Simulator). The results of the Unit Tests should not depend on the targer. Unit Tests are limited to the available RAM, ROM size of the selected target.

help.title: Logs Editor
help.officialContent:
How to create logs Add from project context menu: Add / Add logs configurator:
Logs User Interface After create or open a logs file,the main view appears.It contains 3 areas:
1 - List of the Logs 2 - List of the variables 3 - Property grid List of the Logs It shows the list of the logs configurators belonging to the current project.
On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Add log Add a new log,the default log type is Periodic; Remove log Remove the selected log; Duplicate log Duplicate the selected log; Property Display the properties of the selected log on the property grid; Add new variable Add new variable; Remove variable Remove the selected variable; Import log Import log; Export log Export log; Memory size Display the total memory size of the selected log; List of the variables This view collects the informations about the variables published by a log.
It collects the informations of name, datatype,UoM and description for each variable.
Property grid It shows the main properties of the log.
Different properties are shown according to the type of log (Change,Dynamic,Expression,Periodic or Threshold).
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current log.
How to enable logs invoke Logs.Check(); exactly when you need to sample. Condition will be evaluated (sample time or trigger), if true a sample will be generated.
sampling will be performed inside the function Check().
typically, invoke the Check() function inside regulation task at every program loop.
Log Types Periodic the variables are sampled according to the sampling period. Threshold sampling is triggered when the threshold is exceeded (greater equal). It is possible to specify the hysteresis, the front, and whether or not to log the reenter event (less). The border value is included in the band. Change sampling takes on the “change” of the value. It is possible to specify a change delta (threshold). Expression sampling is performed as long as the specified boolean expression remains true. Dynamic log memory is reserved, but log it is not defined. It will be possible to configure it later at commissioning time, without necessarily to re-compile the application. You won’t be able to add expression type logs. How to retrieve logs STone: on target, retrieve/logs.There are two log format:
1 .json to send data on cloud
2 .csv to import data in a datasheet
Log API 1. Logs.GetConfig(id) : LogConfig Gets the specified log information by log id. The following struct (LogConfig) will be returned:
LogConfig : STRUCT Id : UINT; Kind : LogKind; SampleLength : UDINT; SamplesCount : UDINT; EntriesCount : UDINT; Properties : LogProperties; END_STRUCT; 2. Logs.Count() Gets the overall number of log
3. Logs.GetLog(id, sampleId, timeStamp, values, valuesTypes) : LogStatus Retrieve sampleId sample of specified id log.The return value indicates the request status:
LogStatus : ( Ok, InvalidMemory, OutOfMemory, Loading, NotInitialized, InvalidLogId, InvalidSampleId, PendingRequest ); 4. Logs.StartStopLog(id, startStop) Log can be started/stopped using the api StartStopLog
5. Logs.ChangeLog(id, config, entries) Changes the configuration and entries of a log
6. Logs.Check() Checks all logs condition and, if verified, adds a log sample.
7. Logs.GetEntries(id, entries) Get all entries of a log.

help.title: Manage Libraries
help.officialContent:
Library Manager allows to add, manage and update all libraries in one place:
With Manage Libraries view users can:
List and browse all the available libraries (and versions) from different folders (Package sources), more on “Manage Package sources” below. List all the installed libraries for the current project. Be notified of updates of newer versions of installed libraries. It works by fetching libraries (.stlib file) from selected folders (Package sources).
Overview of Manage Libraries view In Solution Explorer, expand the Dependencies node, right click on Libs node and click Manage Libraries.
The Manage Libraries view will be shown: It mainly consist of two parts, the libraries information list on the left and the libraries managing in the right part.
A search box, above the libraries list, help finding libraries filtering by their name.
Package sources can be changed in the top right, showing in the list only the libraries from the selected source.
Browse Libraries Open the Manage Libraries view, switch to Browse tab, all libraries of the selected Package resource will be shown. In this tab, in the libraries list:
Newer versions libraries are marked with an updatable icon. Installed libraries are marked with a green tick icon. No icon means the libraries is not installed. Behaviors on library when selected from the list:
If a non-installed library is selected, an Install action will be permitted with the Install button in the right part or just with the + icon near the library name. If an installed library selected, and it is a newer version than the installed one, an Update action will be permitted with the Update button in the right part or just with the Updatable icon over the item. If none of above, not actions are permitted. View Installed Libraries of Current Project Open the Manage Libraries view, switch to Installed tab, all installed libraries in current project will be shown. If any of them has a newer version, it will be marked with the Updatable icon, otherwise a green “tick” icon means installed.
View Updatable Libraries of Current Project Updatable libraries appear with a specific icon as showed below:
Open the Manage Libraries view, switch to Update tab, it shows all the updatable libraries installed in current project, if any of them has a newer version. In the right part, all the available versions are listed. And Update action could be performed.
Note: In Update tab, a Downgrade action will be permitted, too
Filtering Libraries Open the Manage Libraries window, switch to any tab, type the desired name in the search box and press Enter, the filtered libraries will be shown. Add and modify Package sources A Package source is a folder (local or network shared) from which the Manage Libraries view will fetch libraries.
Users can add a desired folder, put all their libraries into it, and access them from the Manage Libraries for all projects.
There is already a Default folder path that is read only, it’s under %USERPROFILE%\Documents\STone\Libs.
To add or modify a Package source go to Tools > Options, and switch to Libraries tab.
Press + icon to add a new folder. Press x icon to remove a folder. Click Update List button to update any background modifications of folders. Press Save to save all the changes.

help.title: Modbus and CAREL Client
help.officialContent:
Base concepts - - Template It defines a range of devices (e.g probes, actuators, …) from the point-of-view of the protocol (Modbus or Carel). It defines an indexed list of variables that a particular range of devices is supposed to publish. Device It is an instance of a template class. It represents the server from the point-of-view of a client. It represents a server that can be attached to a line. Line It represents both the transmission channel and the protocol running over the channel from the point-of-view of a client. It contains the informations about the channel (Serial or TcpIp) and about the protocol (Modbus or Carel). It is attached to a list of devices to communicate with. It generates a carillon of commands to send to the devices attached to it. Command It represents the request sent over the protocol to a specific device during a poll-step of the carillon. Carillon It represents the collection of commands continously performed by a client, according to the actions defined in the template and according to the devices attached to the line. It is composed by a list of poll-steps. Configurator It represents the environment in which you configure client protocols. It collects all the configurations of clients in the .stmp file. Configuration It represents an instance of line. Task Each protocol configuration (line) will run asynchronously in a specific event-driven task. Client configurator The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the client configurations.
Line configurator Choosing the Clients tab of the client configurators, UI shows:
1 - Navigation tree of the lines 2 - List of the not-yet-bound devices 3 - Property grid 1. Navigation tree of the lines It shows the list of the client configurations belonging to the current project.
It shows the list of the devices bound to the respective line.
The Modbus configurations have the icon: The Carel configurations have the icon: Near by the name there are rapid informations about the configuration:
For serial supervisors, in brackets, the respective COM port is displayed. For TcpIp supervisors, in brackets, the respective protocol (TCP or UDP) and port are displayed. On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a server configuration Delete the focused client configuration Import an existing client configuration Export the focused client configuration Define the task priority (Advanced) Display the properties of the focused element (line configuration or device) on the property grid 2. List of the not-yet-bound devices This view collects all the instances of template (devices) declared in the code and available-to-bind.
The Modbus devices have the icon: The Carel devices have the icon: 3. Property grid It shows the main properties of the configuration or of the device (depending on the focused element).
Different properties are shown according to the type of the element (Serial or TcpIp).
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current client configuration or device.
The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the client configurations.
Template configurator Choosing the Templates tab of the client configurators, UI shows:
1 - List of the templates 2 - List of the variables published by the focused template 3 - Property grid 1. List of the templates It shows the list of the templates belonging to the current project.
Near by the name there are rapid informations about the template.
The Modbus templates have the icon: The Carel templates have the icon: On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a template Delete the focused template Import an existing template Export the focused template Display the properties of the focused template on the property grid 2. List of the variables published by the focused template This view collects the informations about the variables published by a device belonging to the focused template class.
It collects all the informations about the variables-to-poll.
It is possible to set any property of a variable.
On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Define a new variable-to-poll as a holding register (only for Modbus templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as an input register (only for Modbus templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as a coil status (only for Modbus templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as a input status (only for Modbus templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as an analog (only for Carel templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as an integer (only for Carel templates) Define a new variable-to-poll as a digital (only for Carel templates) Sort the variables by type (registers, coils) and index Copy the selected variables Paste the selected variables Delete the selected variables Show the advanced settings for the variables Notes about templates memory for declared variables The protocol engine (Modbus or Carel) needs an internal memory where to store a copy of the protocol data. This memory is defined for each kind (e.g. Analog for CAREL protocol, HoldingRegister for Modbus) starting from the lowest index to the highest index defined.
The Modbus standard allows only contiguous registers definition.
Example:
In a Modbus Template, if a Holding Register is defined at index 5 and another one is defined at index 50, the memory for 46 registers is allocated.
3. Property grid It shows the main properties of the focused template.
Different properties are shown according to the type of template (Modbus or Carel).
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current template.
How to configure a client In order to configure a client protocol you need to:
Add the client protocol configurator Create a line configuration Define a Template Publish the variables Create a device Bind the devices to the line Add the client protocol configurator After creating a STone project, it is possible to add a client configurator.
In the “Solution explorer” tab, right-click on the name of the project and choose Add => Add client protocols configurator.
In the solution will be created the file “ClientProtocols.stsp” and the editor will open.
Create a line configuration Open the client protocols configurator.
Choose the “Clients” tab.
Click the “Add configuration” button The wizard will open.
Follow the instructions and configure with the proper settings.
Remember to copy-and-paste in the main program the block of code in the last page of the wizard in order to make the just-created protocol task run.
It is possible to edit the property of a configuration using the property grid.
The properties of a line configuration, shown in property grid too, are: Name is the configuration’s name Protocol is the configuration’s protocol (Read Only) Bits are the used serial bits (only for serial configurations) Parity is the used serial parity (only for serial configurations) Speed is the serial baudrate (only for serial configurations) Stop Bits are the used serial stop bits (only for serial configurations) Port is the communication serial port or TcpIp port (respectively for serial and TcpIp configurations) Protocol is the TcpIp protocol (only for TcpIp configurations) Detection Range is the time to wait when retrying to poll an offline device Polling Delay is the time between two poll cycles Retry is the number of retries executed if a device’s answer is not received Define a template Open the client protocols configurator.
Choose the “Templates” tab.
Click the “Add template” button and choose the appropriate protocol from the drop-down menu that will appear.
Write the template name in the text-box that will appear.
An empty template editor will appear.
It is possible to edit the property of a configuration using the property grid.
The properties of a template, shown in property grid too, are: Name is the template’s name Protocol is the protocol of the template (Read Only) Action is the action performed when the answer of a ReportServerId command is received from a device belonging to the template (only for Modbus templates) Read mode is the read mode of the ReportServerId command (only for Modbus templates) Read coil points is the maximum number of coils read when a read command is performed (only for Modbus templates) Read register points is the maximum number of registers read when a read command is performed (only for Modbus templates) Write coil points is the maximum number of coils written when a write command is performed (only for Modbus templates) Write register points is the maximum number of registers written when a write command is performed (only for Modbus templates) Write analog points is the maximum number of analogs written when a write command is performed (only for Carel templates) Write integer points is the maximum number of integers written when a write command is performed (only for Carel templates) Write digital points is the maximum number of digital written when a write command is performed (only for Carel templates) Define the variables-to-poll Open the client protocols configurator.
Choose the “Templates” tab.
Focus an existing template from the list of the templates. The view of the variables-to-poll will appear.
Using the appropriate buttons on top of the tab, add the variables-to-poll onto the template.
Edit the properties of the variables.
It is possible to edit the property of a variable using the variables table.
The properties of a published variable, shown in the table, are: Name is the variable’s name Type is the variable’s type of data (e.g. INT, UINT, REAL, CHAR, …) CommunicationType is the type of data from the protocol point-of-view (e.g. HoldingRegister, CoilStatus, …) Size is the number of registers used to transmit the value of the variable (e.g. 1 register for a INT-variable, 2 registers for a REAL-variable, …) Index is the starting index of the protocol where the variable is transmitted RWMode tells the protocol-commands related to the variable (e.g. ReadPollWriteChange, ReadOnlineNoWrite, NoReadWriteChangeWriteOnline, …) Protected is the visibility of the variable within the application (i.e. PROTECTED if ticked, PUBLIC otherwise) Clicking the button, additional columns will appear. (see Advanced) Advanced The additional properties that will show up are: UoM is the unit-of-measure-attribute attached to the variable Persistence is the persistence of the variable within the application (i.e. retain or none) Enable is the name of the field of template’s instance that enables the protocol-commands over the variable Callback is the function that is runned whenever a valid answer to a read-command of the variable is received (only for Modbus templates) Description is the description of the variable displayed as a tool-tip Hysteresis is the minimum change that must occur to the value of the variable in order to be marked as “changed” (only for Carel templates) Create a device Once that a template is defined, after compiling, it will be possible to instanciate a device belonging to the template class.
To create template instances (devices) there are several ways:
Declare as global variables Declare as Function Block VAR PUBLIC variable Extend a Function Block, Class or Program, using EXTENDS keyword After compiling, the just-created devices will appear in the view of the not-yet-bound devices.
It is possible to edit the property of a device using the property grid.
The properties of a device, shown in property grid too, are: Name is the device’s name (Read Only) Command Delay is the time between two polling commands Detection Timeout is the timeout to wait for an answer when the device is offline Enabled is the device’s starting status (Enabled or Disabled) Ident is the device’s address Network Address is the device’s IP address or hostname (only if the device is bound to a TcpIp line) Timeout is the device’s timeout to wait for an answer when the device is online Zone is the device’s Unit Conversion Zone Bind the devices to a line Open the client protocols configurator.
Choose the “Clients” tab.
Drag-and-drop the device icon over the desired line configuration, releasing the mouse button when the “Move” tool-tip appear.
In the navigation tree the device now will appear bound to the line, while it will disappear from the “Device” view.
Edit the properties of the device.
Properties of the Line Instance Since the line is an instance of an object, a number of properties and methods are available.
The properties and methods of an instance of a line configuration are: The method Init initializes the line The method Read updates the values of devices’ variables with the values stored in the protocol memory The method Write writes the values of devices’ variables on the protocol memory The method Start starts the client protocol The method Stop stops the client protocol The method IsRunning returns TRUE if the line is running The field SerialSettings contains the serial settings of the line The field TcpIpSettings contains the tcp-ip settings of the line The method ChangeSettings applies the current settings The field CustomCommand manages the transmission of custom commands (see Advanced) The field Info is a structure containing all the informations of the line (see Advanced) Advanced The fields of the Info struct are: The field DetectionRange is the default detection range of a device (s) The field PollingDelay is the default polling delay (ms) The field Retry is the default command retry count The field LineType is the type of line (Serial, TcpIp) The field LastPollingLoopTime is the duration of the last polling loop The field PollingLoopsNumber is the total count of polling loops since the line started The methods of the CustomCommand class are: The method AnswerReceived tells if an answer to the previous custom command was received The method SendCustomCommand transmits the custom command over the protocol Properties of the Device Since the device is an instance of an object, a number of properties and methods are available.
The properties and methods of an instance of a device are: The fields named after the names of variables by which you can access (R/W) the value of the respective variable The field Enable is a structure containing all the enablers defined in the template’s class The field Info is a structure containing all the informations of the device (see below) The method Init initializes the device according to the settings passed by argument The method ChangeIdent assigns the ident passed by argument to the device The method ChangeNetworkAddress assigns the network address (IP or hostname) passed by argument to the device The method Read updates the values of variables’ fields of the device with the values stored in the protocol memory The method Write writes the values of variables’ fields of the device on the protocol memory Other advanced methods are available (see “Advanced”) Advanced The fields of the Info struct are: The method RunCallback runs the callback-actions (related to a specific poll step) defined in the template configurator The method Get_Input_Register retrieves raw value of an input register given its index (to call only from a callback) The method Get_Holding_Register retrieves raw value of a holding register given its index (to call only from a callback) The method Get_Coil_Status retrieves raw value of a coil status given its index (to call only from a callback) The method Get_Input_Status retrieves raw value of an input status given its index (to call only from a callback) The method Get_IR_Count gets the number of input registers defined in the template The method Get_HR_Count gets the number of holding registers defined in the template The method Get_CS_Count gets the number of coils status defined in the template The method Get_IS_Count gets the number of input status defined in the template The method Get_IR_Info gets the index of an input register given its position in the IR table The method Get_HR_Info gets the index of a holding register given its position in the HR table The method Get_CS_Info gets the index of a coil status given its position in the CS table The method Get_IS_Info gets the index of an input status given its position in the IS table The informations contained in the field Info of a device instance are: The field Ident is the ident of the device The field IsOnline tells if the device is online or offline The field Enabled enables or disables the device The field CommandDelay is the command delay (ms) of the device The field DetectionTimeout is the detection timeout (ms) of the device The field Timeout is the timeout (ms) of the device The field Zone is the zone of the device (No, SI, Imperial) Other advanced fields are available (see “Advanced”) Advanced The fields of the Info struct are: The field PollsCount counts the number of times in which the client complete the cycle of read/write commands list with the device The field CommandsCount counts the number of times in which the client send a command with the device The field ReadChangesCount counts the number of times data is updated from a device The field DeviceError is the current device error The field ErrorsCount counts the number of times in which the field DeviceError changed its value The field LastErrorInfo contains the informations about to the last error received from the device The field forceMultipleCoilWrite forces the client to use only the 15-command as write-coils-command (only Modbus devices) The field forceMultipleRegisterWrite forces the client to use only the 16-command as write-registers-command (only Modbus devices) The field forceMultipleAnalogsWrite forces the client to use only the S-command as write-analog-command (only Carel devices) The field forceMultipleDigitalsWrite forces the client to use only the B-command as write-digitals-command (only Carel devices) The field forceMultipleIntegersWrite forces the client to use only the U-command as write-integers-command (only Carel devices) Advanced features Define a Callback Open the client protocols configurator and choose the “Templates” tab.
Choose the desired template from the list and expand the columns of the variables’ view.
For each variable a callback can be defined by writing the name of the corresponding action in the “Callback” column.
An already-existing action can be assigned, or a new callback action can be defined.
If a new callback was defined, a pop-up will show up.
After clicking on “Ok”, a new .st file, named after the callback, will be created in the project folder in the Protocols > Actions path.
Open the just-created file and define the behaviour of the callback.
Compile in order to get the changes applied.
Define a ReportServerId action Open the client protocols configurator and choose the “Templates” tab.
Choose the desired template from the list and click .
In the property grid, the action and the corresponding read-mode can be defined.
An already-existing action can be assigned, or a new action can be defined.
If a new action was defined, a pop-up will show up.
After clicking on “Ok”, a new .st file, named after the action, will be created in the project folder in the Protocols > Actions path.
Open the just-created file and define the behaviour of the action.
Compile in order to get the changes applied.
Define an Enable for a variable Open the client protocols configurator and choose the “Templates” tab.
Choose the desired template from the list and expand the columns of the variables’ view.
For each variable an enable can be defined by writing the name of the corresponding enable in the “Enable” column.
An already-existing enable can be assigned, or a new enable can be defined.
Compile in order to get the changes applied.
Now the value of the enable can be changed exploring the field Enable of a device belonging to the corresponding template.
Use of the method Init Since the method initializes an object, the method must be called before of any other instruction and any other modification, as follows: First of all call the method Init, so that the object is initialized with the values specified in the property grid Once the object is initialized, apply any method or modification that is needed Note that the behaviour of the method “Init” is the same for both client and server configurations.
Any modification applied before the call of method Init will be lost.
Use of the method ChangeSettings Since the method simply applies the current settings, the method must be called after the modification of the settings, as follows: First of all define the new settings by accessing the settings field Once the new settings are defined, call the method ChangeSettings in order to apply the new settings Note that the behaviour of the method “ChangeSettings” is the same for both client and server configurations.
Clarifications Timings The following notations have been used throughout the code: Detection internal is the so-called field “Detection range” among the properties of the line Detection timeout is the so-called field “Detection timeout” among the properties of the device Timeout is the so-called field “Timeout” among the properties of the device N Retries is the so-called field “Retry” among the properties of the line The following notations have been used throughout the code: Command delay is the so-called field “Command delay” among the properties of the device R/W Modes The R/W Modes are defined as follows: ReadOnlineNoWrite: read the value when the device gets online from an offline status ReadPollNoWrite: read the variable in every polling cycle NoReadWriteChange: write the variable if the value is changed in the application ReadOnlineWriteChange: read the value when the device gets online from an offline status and write it if it changed in the application ReadPollWriteChange: read the variable in every polling cycle and write it if it changed in the application NoReadWriteChangeWriteOnline: write the variable if the value is changed in the application and force the value in the application when the device gets online from an offline status ReadPollWriteChangeWriteOnline: read the variable in every polling cycle, write the variable if the value is changed in the application and force the value in the application when the device gets online from an offline status NoReadWritePoll: write the variable in every polling cycle Zones The Zone attribute sets the automatic conversion for all the variables exchanged via protocols, as defined below: NO: no conversion is applied SI: convert and publish all the variables in units of the international-system (according to the UoM) Imperial: convert and publish all the variables in units of the imperial system (according to the UoM) Device Errors The Device Errors are defined as follows: NoError: Device answered as expected Offline: Device did not answer (offline) InvalidPacket: Device answered with an invalid packet ErrorCodeReceived: Device answered with an error code NotYetQueried: Device has yet to be queried BadPDU: Device answered with too short PDU BadCRC: Device answered with a wrong CRC IllegalData: Device answered with an invalid data UnsupportedFunction: Device answered with an unsupported function code UnexpectedFunction: Device answered with a different function code from that expected UnexpectedData: Device answered with different number of data from that expected ReceivedDataOutOfRange: Device answered with out of range data ErrorInfo struct The fields of struct ErrorInfo are defined as follows: The field ErrorCode is the (raw) error code returned by the device (see Modbus standard for more info) The field FunctionCode is the function code that generates the error The field StartingRegister is the starting register of the function that generates the error The field RegistersCount is the number of registers involved on function that generates the error
