help.title: Solution
help.officialContent:
Solution class This class represent a STone solution.
Solution is part of the stone object which is already present when running the python script.
Solution is an object that includes within it the class Projects.
Projects is an array with all the projects of the solution (see more in the “Project” page).
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") For obtain a valid STone solution, you could call the method CreateNewSolution:
solution = stone.Solution basedir = 'c:/path/to/your/solution' sln_name = 'TestSolution' tmpl_name = 'BaseProject' # Create a new solution result, sln_file = solution.CreateNewSolution(basedir, sln_name, tmpl_name) # Check the result if result.IsSuccessful: print(sln_file) # Output: c:\path\to\your\solution\TestSolution\TestSolution.stone solution.Open(sln_file) else: # Try to log something print('Creation error:%s' % result.Errors[0].Description) Fields Field Data type Description Projects Array[Project] List of all projects contained in the currently open solution. ActiveSolutionConfiguration SolutionConfiguration The current active solution configuration of the currently open solution. SolutionConfigurations Array[SolutionConfiguration] The list of solution configurations of the currently open solution. Example: Since Projects is a list, you can cycle it with a for.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": # ... Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
Open(solutionPath)Description:
Open and loads a STone solution.
The solution must be opened before calling any other methods like save, compile, etc…
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description solutionPath string The full path of the “.stone” solution file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Solution.stone” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") Close()Description:
Close the currently open STone solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Close the stone solution stone.Solution.Close() Save()Description:
Save the currently open STone solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Save the stone solution stone.Solution.Save() SetActiveProject(projectName)Description:
Set projectName as the Active project of the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project contained it the currently open solution.
e.g. “pCOProject1” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Set "pGD1Prj1" as the active project stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("pGD1Prj1") CreateNewProject(templateName, baseDir, projectName)Description:
Create a new project starting from a project template.
The new project will be created in the folder specified by baseDir with projectName as its name.
templateName can be one of the following:
(Note that related plugins must be installed)
“BaseProject” “EmptyProject” “pCOProject” “pGD1Prj” “SevenSegmentsPrj” Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description templateName string The name of the template on which the project is to be based.
e.g. “BaseProject” baseDir string The absolute path in which to create the project.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\” projectName string The name to give to the new project. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Create a new project named "MyProjectName" based on "BaseProject" stone.Solution.CreateNewProject("BaseProject", "C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Project\\", "MyProjectName") CreateNewSolution(baseDir, name, templateName = "BaseProject")Description:
Create a solution with a template project, the solution name is specified by the parameter name. The new solution will be created under the directory baseDir. You should be aware that a folder with the same name with the solution will be created in baseDir.
The project type is specified by the parameter templateName, which is just same usage with the parameter in CreateNewProject. The possible values will be like following: (Note that related plugins must be installed)
“BaseProject” “EmptyProject” “pCOProject” “pGD1Prj” “SevenSegmentsPrj” Returns:
A tuple with (IResult, string), which gives errors in IResult member and the solution path in string member
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description baseDir string The absolute path in which to create the solution.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\” name string The name of the solution. templateName string The name of the template on which the project is to be based.
e.g. “BaseProject” Example:
solution = stone.Solution # Create a new solution result, sln_file = solution.CreateNewSolution( 'c:/your/solution', 'TestSolution', 'BaseProject' ) if result.IsSuccessful: print(sln_file) else: print(result.Errors[0].Description) AddExistingProject(fileName)Description:
Adds an existing project to the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description fileName string The absolute path of the “.stprj” project file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Project.stprj” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Add "ExistingProject" to solution stone.Solution.AddExistingProject("C:\\Path\\To\\Other\\Solution\\ExistingProject\\ExistingProject.stprj") RemoveProject(projectName, delete = false)Description:
Removes an existing project from the currently open solution.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project contained it the currently open solution.
e.g. “pCOProject1” delete bool If true, delete the project folder. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Remove "ExistingProject" from solution stone.Solution.RemoveProject("ExistingProject") Build()Description:
Compiles the currently open solution.
Returns:
Returns a Result object. Result.IsSuccessful = True if successful and there is no build error, false otherwise and lists “Result.Errors”, “Result.Warning”, “Result.Messages” if any.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Build the solution stone.Solution.Build() SetActiveSolutionConfiguration(solutionConfiguration)Description:
Sets the active solution configuration.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if configuration does not exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description solutionConfiguration SolutionConfiguration The solution configuration to set as the active solution configuration.
Tip: SolutionConfigurations field of Solution class is a list of all the available solution configurations. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Sets Debug as the active solution configuration for configuration in stone.Solution.SolutionConfigurations: if configuration.Name == "Debug": stone.Solution.SetActiveSolutionConfiguration(configuration)

help.title: Unit Tests Explorer
help.officialContent:
Use the Unit Tests Explorer to run Unit Tests from STone IDE.
After running the tests, Unit Tests Explorer will show the results of the execution, eventual error message and stack trace, and other info in the Test Info View.
You can also use Unit Tests Explorer to Debug Unit Tests and to Analyze Code Coverage.
Run tests in Unit Tests Explorer Open the Unit Tests Explorer from “Test > Unit Tests Explorer”.
All tests of the current active project will be shown.
It is possible run them by clicking on the button or with the shortcut CTRL + U.
After the execution ended it is possible to see the results for each individual test.
Unit Tests Explorer is composed of 3 main parts:
Toolbar Tests Tree List Test Info View 1. Toolbar Run All. Execute all Unit Tests. Run. Execute the selected Unit Tests. The popup menu contains other commands. Repeat Last Run. Executes again the last Unit Tests run. Run Failed Tests. Executes the tests with Failed status. Analyze Code Coverage for All Tests. Test Counters. Counters with the number of total tests, passed tests, failed tests and not run tests. Expand All. Expand all tests in the Test Tree List. Collapse All. Collapse all tests in the Test Tree List. Options. Code Coverage settings (See Code Coverage page) and default target settings. Search Bar. Search through the tests in the Test Tree List Run popup menu:
Within the run popup menu it is possible to run Unit Tests, Debug them, clear tests status and results, and Analyze the Code Coverage for all the tests.
To debug a test it is sufficient to place a break point in the desired line and click on a debug command of the run popup menu.
2. Test Tree List The Test Tree List shows all the test of the currently active project.
They are grouped by Test Suites which contains Test Cases.
It is possible to see test status, test name, number of containing tests for Test Suites, test execution Duration and the Error Message if a test has failed.
It is possible to navigate the tree list with CTRL + right/left arrow key to open/close a node, holding shift and move with arrow keys to select multiple tests or holding CTRL and click on desired tests to select them.
Double clicking on a test opens the test location in the ST editor.
By right clicking on a test it is possible to run, debug, go to definition, or analyze the code coverage of the selected test.
By clicking on a test it is possible to view additional info in the Test Info View below.
3. Test Info View In the Test Info View it is possible to view additional info for Test Suites and Test Cases:
Test Suite Summary Within the Test Suite Summary it is possible to see the suite name, number of Test Cases contained, relative Location of the Test Suite class definition, collective test duration and the class comment documentation.
Test Case Summary Within the Test Case Summary it is possible to see the test name, relative Location of the Test Case method definition, test duration and the method comment documentation.
If the test status is failed it is possible to also view the error message (assert failed, array out of bound, etc…) and the stack trace with information on the POUs and the file locations.
Unit Tests Status Status Icon Status Meaning Not Run Test Test Passed Test Failed Test waiting for run Test is running Integration with ST Editor It is possible to take advantage of the integration between Unit Tests Explorer and ST Editor to run and view the states of Unit Tests from Code Lens
In particular, an icon is visible above the unit tests methods, which, when clicked, causes a popup to appear, allowing interaction with the Unit Tests Explorer by running tests.
Depending on the test result, whether it was positive or negative, the icon changes and by clicking the popup you can see the execution time and the stacktrace, if any.
In the methods that are referenced by Unit Tests, on the other hand, it is possible to see the status of those methods, and to execute the tests that are plausibly impacted by the modification of that method.

help.title: Web Pages
help.officialContent:
STone allows displaying Web pages and test them as they were served by the c.PCO (and other selected programmable controllers) integrated Webserver.
In order to enable Web pages testing, folders containing the Web pages have to be configured as Virtual Directories.
Add and modify Virtual Directories A Virtual Directory is a folder (local or network shared) from which STone PC-Simulator will fetch and serve web pages.
To add or modify a Virtual Directory go to Tools->Options and switch to Simulation tab.
Make sure that the PC-Simulator is stopped. Press + Add Virtual Directory button to add a new folder. Press - button beside an entry to remove a folder. Press Save to save all the changes. Note Up to 10 different Virtual Directories can be configured. The default home page is index.html, please make sure that the selected folder contains it. Virtual Directories names should be unique Virtual Directories can only contain alphanumerical characters without whitespaces and other special characters Display Web pages Once at least a Virtual Directory is configured, Web pages can be shown from the STone Main Toolbar
Make sure the PC-Simulator is started, select the desired Virtual Directory from the menu and they will automatically appear in the default web browser

help.title: BACnet Client
help.officialContent:
Base concepts - - Template It defines a range of devices (e.g probes, actuators, …) from the point-of-view of the protocol (BACnet). It defines an indexed list of BACnet objects that a particular range of devices is supposed to publish. Device It is an instance of a template class. It represents the server from the point-of-view of a client. It represents a server that can be attached to a line. Line It represents both the transmission channel and the protocol running over the channel from the point-of-view of a client. It contains the informations about the channel and about the protocol (BACnet). It is attached to a list of devices to communicate with. It generates a carillon of commands to send to the devices attached to it. Configurator It represents the environment in which you configure client protocols. It collects all the configurations of clients in the .stmp file. Configuration It represents an instance of line. Task Each protocol configuration (line) will run asynchronously in a specific event-driven task. BACnet BACnet (Building and Control Network) is the global data communication standard for building automation and control networks. BACnet Device A BACnet Device is the network-visible representation of control equipment connected to a BACnet network, which responds to BACnet service requests. A Device represents the control equipment by maintaining a collection of BACnet Objects. BACnet Object BACnet object(s) are concepts that allow the communication and organization of data related to inputs, outputs, software, and calculations to be performed. The BACnet Object can manifest itself in a variety of ways. Supported BACnet Objects are: DeviceObject, AnalogInput, AnalogOutput, AnalogValue, BinaryInput, BinaryOutput, BinaryValue, MultiStateInput, MultiStateOutput, MultiStateValue, CharacterString, IntegerValue, PositiveIntegerValue, NotificationClass. The Objects within any Device are uniquely identified by an Object type and by an instance number (together these data make up an Object Identifier). Each Device must contain one Device Object to represent the BACnet capabilities of the Device. BACnet Object Properties The Objects contain Properties that can be accessed and manipulated using BACnet’s Read-Property and Write-Property service requests. Client is also a server In bacnet, client is not only a client, but act also as server, since the network should be a multi-master network, where potentially, all devices can be a client.
So by default, the server side of a client is a device with only DeviceObject and a NotificationClass, both with instance 1.
But if the user wants, he can attach an existing server configuration when he calls the Start method.
So the flow is:
Example:
# Initialize the client but do not start it Line_1.Init(FALSE); # Initialize the server but do not start it Supervisor_1.Init(FALSE); # Start the client, using BACnet Server 'Supervisor_1' configuration as Server model Line_1.Start(Supervisor_1); Client configurator The editor permits to have the control of all single parts of the client configurations.
1 - Navigation tree of the lines 2 - List of the not-yet-bound devices 3 - Property grid 1. Navigation tree of the lines It shows the list of the client configurations belonging to the current project.
It shows the list of the devices bound to the respective line.
The BACnet configurations have the icon: Near by the name there are rapid informations about the configuration:
For serial supervisors, in brackets, the respective COM port is displayed. For IP supervisors, in brackets, the respective protocol (UDP) and port are displayed. On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a client configuration Import an existing client configuration Delete the focused client configuration Define the task priority Display the properties of the focused client configuration on the property grid 2. List of the not-yet-bound devices This view collects all the instances of template (devices) declared in the code and available-to-bind.
The BACnet devices have the icon: 3. Property grid It shows the main properties of the configuration.
Different properties are shown according to the type of configuration.
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current client configuration.
Template configurator Choosing the Templates tab of the client configurators, UI shows:
1 - List of the templates 2 - List of the BACnet objects published by the focused template 3 - List of properties of the selected object 4 - Property grid 1. List of the templates It shows the list of the templates belonging to the current project.
Near by the name there are rapid informations about the template.
The BACnet templates have the icon: On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a template Delete the focused template Import an existing template Export the focused template Display the properties of the focused template on the property grid 2. List of the BACnet objects published by the focused template This view collects the informations about the objects published by a device belonging to the focused template class.
It collects all the informations about the objects-to-poll.
It is possible to choose name, description and instance for each object.
It is possible to set any property of a objects.
On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Define a new objects-to-poll as any of the standards BACnet objects from the given list Available objects are: DeviceObject AnalogInput AnalogOutput AnalogValue BinaryInput BinaryOutput BinaryValue MultiStateInput MultiStateOutput MultiStateValue CharacterString IntegerValue PositiveIntegerValue NotificationClass Sort the objects by type (AnalogInput, AnalogOutput) and index Copy the selected objects Paste the selected objects Delete the selected objects Show the advanced settings for the objects 3. List of properties of the selected object On the left side of the object row there is a “+” icon.
Clicking on it expands the list of all the properties supported by the related object.
This view collects the informations about the properties published by a single object.
For each property:
Enable/Disable Poll of the object property Select the Read/Write mode Mode Description ReadPoll - NoWrite Read the variable every polling cycle. ReadPoll - WriteChange Read the variable every polling cycle and write it if changed in the application. ReadPoll - WriteChange - WriteOnline Read the variable every polling cycle, write it if changed in the application and force the value in the application when the device return from offline\is online for the first time. NoRead - WriteChange Write the variable if the value is changed in the application. NoRead - WritePoll Write the variable every polling cycle. NoRead - WriteChange - WriteOnline Write the variable if the value is changed in the application and force the value in the application when the device return from offline\is online for the first time. ReadOnline - NoWrite Read the value when the device return from offline\is online for the first time. ReadOnline - WriteChange Read the value when the device return from offline and write it if changed in the application. Read COV - NoWrite Read the variable by subscribing a COV. Read COV- WriteChange Read the variable by subscribing a COV and write it if changed in the application. Read COV- WriteChange - WriteOnline Read the variable by subscribing a COV, write it if changed in the application and force the value in the application when the device return from offline\is online for the first time. COV = “Change Of Value” 4. Property grid It shows the main properties of the template.
ReadPoints are the number of points readable on one read command request.
WritePoints are the number of points writable on one write command request.
How To Configure A Client Refer to Modbus and CAREL Client section
BACnet client: limitations on the number of objects There is a strict limit on the number of object that can be added to a monitored device in the BACnet client editor. As in the server, the number of object that can be added is strongly dependent on the type of devices. In the following table, the objects are grouped into three different object types (differently from the server application, all the low footprint objects are grouped together).
The object types maximum number supported by the client is listed in the third column. Please note that this number is referred to the whole client, i.e. the maximum number of objects used in all the monitored devices must not exceed it.
Obj Name Classification Max objects Analog Objects (I/O/V) Binary Objects (I/O/V) Integer Value Positive Integer Value File Calendar Notification Class Standard object Low footprint + Advanced object - Low footprint 100 Multistate Objects (I/O/V) Standard object - High footprint 64 Characterstring Value Standard Object - Very High footprint 32 The maximum number of devices that can be added to a client editor is 32.

help.title: BACnet Server
help.officialContent:
Base concepts - - Supervisor It represents both the transmission channel and the protocol running over the channel from the point-of-view of a server. It contains the informations about the channel (Serial or UDP) and about the protocol (BACnet). It publishes a list of objects over the protocol. It is unaware of the presence of a client. Configurator It represents the environment in which you configure server protocols. It collects all the configurations of servers in the .stsp file. Configuration It represents an instance of supervisor. Task Each protocol configuration (supervisor) will run asynchronously in a specific event-driven task. BACnet BACnet (Building and Control Network) is the global data communication standard for building automation and control networks. BACnet Device A BACnet Device is the network-visible representation of control equipment connected to a BACnet network, which responds to BACnet service requests. A Device represents the control equipment by maintaining a collection of BACnet Objects. BACnet Object BACnet object(s) are concepts that allow the communication and organization of data related to inputs, outputs, software, and calculations to be performed. The BACnet Object can manifest itself in a variety of ways. Supported BACnet Objects are: DeviceObject, AnalogInput, AnalogOutput, AnalogValue, BinaryInput, BinaryOutput, BinaryValue, MultiStateInput, MultiStateOutput, MultiStateValue, CharacterString, IntegerValue, PositiveIntegerValue, NotificationClass. The Objects within any Device are uniquely identified by an Object type and by an instance number (together these data make up an Object Identifier). Each Device must contain one Device Object to represent the BACnet capabilities of the Device. BACnet Object Properties The Objects contain Properties that can be accessed and manipulated using BACnet’s Read-Property and Write-Property service requests. Server configurator The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the server configurations.
1 - List of the configurations 2 - List of the objects published by the focused configuration 3 - List of properties of the selected object 4 - Property grid 1. List of the configurations It shows the list of the server configurations belonging to the current project.
The BACnet configurations have the icon: Near by the name there are rapid informations about the configuration:
For serial supervisors, in brackets, the respective COM port is displayed. For IP supervisors, in brackets, the respective protocol (UDP) and port are displayed. On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a server configuration Delete the focused server configuration Import an existing server configuration Export the focused server configuration Define the task priority (Advanced, only for Modbus and CAREL protocols) Display the properties of the focused server configuration on the property grid 2. List of the objects published by the focused configuration This view collects the informations about the objects published by a configuration.
It collects the informations about the specific object.
It is possible to choose name, description and instance for each object.
On top of the tab there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Add an object from the given list Available objects are: DeviceObject AnalogInput AnalogOutput AnalogValue BinaryInput BinaryOutput BinaryValue MultiStateInput MultiStateOutput MultiStateValue CharacterString IntegerValue PositiveIntegerValue NotificationClass There must be 1 DeviceObject and at least 1 NotificationClass objects for each server configuration. These 2 objects are added by default and cannot be removed. Delete the selected objects 3. List of properties of the selected object This view collects the informations about the properties published by a single object.
For each property:
An existing variable can be linked clicking on the ... button. COV (Change of Value notification) can be enabled (a client can subscribe to COV notifications of the selected property) Can be defined if it’s Writable from a client or it’s Read-Only 4. Property grid It shows the main properties of the configuration.
Different properties are shown according to the type of configuration (Serial or IP).
Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the informations about the current server configuration.
How to configure a server In order to configure a BACnet server protocol you need to:
Add the server protocol configurator Create a BACnet server configuration Add the objects to be published (pre-defined variables are not mandatory) Add the server protocol configurator Refer to Modbus and CAREL Server section
Create a server configuration Refer to Modbus and CAREL Server section
The properties of a BACnet server configuration, shown in property grid too, are: Name is the configuration’s name Protocol is the configuration’s protocol (Read Only) Bits are the used serial bits (only for serial configurations) IDE Mode is the serial port IDE access (only for serial configurations) Parity is the used serial parity (only for serial configurations) Speed is the serial baudrate (only for serial configurations) Stop Bits Bits are the used serial stop bits (only for serial configurations) Instance is the server address Port is the communication serial port or UDP port (respectively for serial and IP configurations) Protocol is the UDP protocol (only for IP configurations) Timeout is the timeout to detect when the client becomes offline (only for serial configurations) Publish the objects Each object added in the editor is an object instance of the Supervisor object, and it’s generated by the tool.
The properties of a published object, shown in the table, are: Name is the name of the object instance Description is the description of the object instance Type is the BACnet object type (Read Only) Instance is the instance number where the object is published (1-based) Variable is the name of the variable linked to the object’s Present Value property (Read Only) The properties of a published object properties, shown in the table, are: Property is the name and the ID of the object property (Read Only) Variable is the variable linked to the object property (can be directly written or selected clicking the ... button) Type is the BACnet object property type (Read Only) COV defines if a client can subscribe to COV notifications of the selected property Writable defines if a client can write the value of the selected property, or if it’s Read-Only Properties of the Supervisor Instance Since the supervisor is an instance of an object, a number of properties and methods are available.
Properties Declared objects in editor are generated as Supervisor instance properties and can be found as Supervisor.object ChannelSettings collects the settings (Serial or IP) of the supervisor DeviceInstance is the instance number of the supervisor Methods GetID gets the internal ID of the configuration Init initializes the server according to the settings defined in the property grid and starts the protocol if called without arguments An overload with a BOOL parameter is available in order to initialize only (with FALSE argument) or initialize and start the protocol (with TRUE argument) Read reads the data from the protocol Start starts the server operations Stop stops the server operations Write writes the data onto the protocol BACnet server: limitations on the number of objects There are some limitations on the number of objects that can be added to the server application and it strongly depends on the type of objects to add. In order to give a classification to the objects, they are divided into low and high footprint and into Standard and Advanced objects. The subdivision is shown in the following table. In order not to exceed the maximum available memory, a limit is imposed to the maximum number of objects, basing on their type. The limit for each type of object is written in the table below.
Obj Name Classification Max objects Analog Objects (I/O/V) Binary Objects (I/O/V) Integer Value Positive Integer Value Standard object Low footprint 400 Multistate Objects (I/O/V) Standard object High footprint 90 Characterstring Value Standard Object Very High footprint 16 File Calendar Notification Class Advanced object Low footprint 32 Schedule Advanced object High footprint 4

help.title: Code Coverage
help.officialContent:
Code Coverage is an objective measure that quantifies the extent to which the tests cover the application code.
It is a percentage of how much of the application code is executed while running Unit Tests, which also means that the other missing percent is code definitely not covered by the execution of Unit Tests.
With the Unit Test Explorer is possible to analyze the Code Coverage for the current active project and view detailed coverage percent for each POUs as well as visual indicators in the ST editor if lines of code are covered or not.
Analyze and view Code Coverage From the Unit Tests Explorer click on to analyze the Code Coverage for all tests.
After it’s execution ended, percentages about total coverage and detailed POU coverage can be found on the Code Coverage Results view.
Shows Code Coverage in the current open file. Clear the coverage result. It is also possible to color code POU coverage percentage by right clicking on the desired column and applying Conditional Formatting and / or sort by coverage percentage.
To view detailed Code Coverage results for each line of code in the ST editor, double click the desired POU to open its location.
By clicking on the refresh button, it will be possible to see if a line of code is covered (marked in green) or not covered (marked in red).
The Code Coverage cannot be calculated if a fatal error has occurred such as an array out of bound (Assert failures aren’t fatal error, code coverage can still be calculated).
Configure filter settings Set filter settings from “Unit Tests Explorer > Options > Code Coverage filter settings” and save the project.
POUs from generated/reserved system files are always excluded.
Option Meaning Exclude all libraries POUs Analyze Code Coverage for application POUs excluding POUs inside libraries (default) Include POUs from opened libraries Analyze Code Coverage for application POUs and opened libraries Analyze only POUs from opened libraries Analyze Code Coverage for only POUs of opened libraries It is possible to add the metadata {METADATA EXCLUDE_FROM_CODE_COVERAGE} to a POU (PROGRAM, METHOD, FUNCTION, FUNCTION_BLOCK) to exclude said POU from Code Coverage metric.

help.title: Project
help.officialContent:
Project class This class represent a STone project within a solution.
Project is part of the Solution class. Solution contains an array of all the projects in the STone solution (see more in the “Solution” page).
Note: Open libraries in the solution are projects.
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution, and get the desired project from the Projects array contained in the Solution class:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": # ... Fields Field Data type Description Name string The name of the project. (Read-Only) e.g. “pCOProject1” Path string The absolute path of the project file. (Read-Only) e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Project.stprj” Files Array[string] The list of all absolute paths of all the user files used by the project. (Read-Only)
Note: This does not includes generated and system files. e.g. [“C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Main.st”, …] ActiveProjectConfiguration ProjectConfiguration The current active project configuration. ProjectConfigurations Array[ProjectConfiguration] The list of project configurations. IsLibrary bool True if the project is a library. (Read-Only) Version string The version of the project. (Read-Only) e.g. “1.2.3” Author string The author of the project. Vendor string The vendor of the project. IsActive bool True if the project is the active project of the solution. (Read-Only) GenerateMetadataFile bool If true generate project metadata file on build. Example: Search for open libraries and close them.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for open libraries and close them for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.IsLibrary: project.CloseProject() # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
AddFile(sourceFilePath, relativeDestinationPath = '', link = false, overwrite = false)Description:
Adds an existing file to the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if file already exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description sourceFilePath string The full path of the file to be added.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\File\file.st” relativeDestinationPath string The project relative destination path in which to add the file.
If empty the file will be added to the root of the project folder. (Default: “”) Tip: GetFolderRelativePaths API returns a list of all the project folders e.g. “Sources\Programs” link bool If true, the file will not be copied to the folder (linked file). (Default: false) overwrite bool If true, if a file with the same name already exists, it is overwritten. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and add Main.st file to Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() RemoveFile(filePath)Description:
Removes a file from the project.
Note: The file will be deleted.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and remove Main.st file from Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.RemoveFile("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\MyProjectName\\Sources\\Programs\\Main.st") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() ExcludeFileFromProject(filePath)Description:
Excludes a file from the project. Note: The file will not be deleted.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and exclude Main.st file from Sources\\Programs for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.ExcludeFileFromProject("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\MyProjectName\\Sources\\Programs\\Main.st") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() RenameFile(filePath, newName, overwrite = false)Description:
Renames a file of the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description filePath string The full path to the file. e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\file.st” newName string The new name to give to the file. overwrite bool If true, if a file with the same name already exists, it is overwritten. (Default: false) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Rename all "Main.st" files to "NewName.st" for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for file in project.Files: if file.endswith("Main.st"): project.RenameFile(file, "NewName.st", True) # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() AddLibrary(stlibPath)Description:
Add a library (.stlib file) to the project.
Returns:
The full path to the newly added library on success, otherwise an empty string.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description stlibPath string The full path of the “.stlib” library package file.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Lib\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib” Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" and add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() CloseProject()Description:
Closes the project.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for open libraries and close them for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.IsLibrary: project.CloseProject() # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() GetOrCreateLibsFolder()Description:
Returns the absolute path of the “Libs” folder of the project.
If the folder does not exist it will be created.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Libs”
Example:
import os # Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Update lib IAQ from version 1.0.0 to 2.0.0 for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for subdir, dirs, libs in os.walk(project.GetOrCreateLibsFolder()): for lib in libs: if "IAQ_v.1.0.0" in lib: project.RemoveFile(lib) project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.2.0.0.stlib") stone.Solution.Save() GetLibsNames(getOpened = true, getClosed = true, withVersion = true)Description:
Returns a list of all the libraries of the project.
e.g. [“IAQ_v.1.0.0”, “SystemMenu_v.1.0.1”]
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description getOpened bool If true, open libraries are included in the list. (Default: true) getClosed bool If true, closed libraries are included in the list. (Default: true) withVersion bool If true, libraries ends with version (e.g. “IAQ_v.1.0.0”) else includes only the name (e.g. “IAQ”). (Default: true) Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search libs in all project for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for lib in project.GetLibsNames() # ... GetFolderRelativePaths()Description:
Returns all relative paths of user project folders.
Note: This does not includes reserved folders.
e.g. [“Gui”, “Images”, “Sources”, “Gui\Actions”, “Gui\CustomMasks”, “Sources\Programs”, …]
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Loop through all folders contained in Sources\\ folder for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for folder in project.GetFolderRelativePaths(): if folder.startswith("Sources\\"): # ... GetOutputDir()Description:
Returns the path to the output directory of the build.
e.g. “C:\Path\To\Solution\Project\Output\Resource1\Configuration1”
Example:
import os bin_files = [] # Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Populate bin_files with all paths to application bin files for project in stone.Solution.Projects: stone.Solution.SetActiveProject(project.Name) stone.Solution.Build() bin_files.append(os.path.join(project.GetOutputDir(), 'flash.bin')) SetActiveProjectConfiguration(projectConfiguration)Description:
Sets the active project configuration.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise or if configuration does not exist.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectConfiguration ProjectConfiguration The project configuration to set as the active project configuration.
Tip: ProjectConfigurations field of Project class is a list of all the available project configurations. Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Sets Debug as the active project configuration for project in stone.Solution.Projects: for configuration in project.ProjectConfigurations: if configuration.Name == "Debug": project.SetActiveProjectConfiguration(configuration)

help.title: Project Configuration
help.officialContent:
ProjectConfiguration class This class represent a configurations of a STone project within a solution.
They are the same configuration that can be found on Build configuration view of project.
Project is part of the Solution class.
Solution contains an array of all the projects in the STone solution (see more in the “Solution” page).
Before calling any other method, first you need to open a valid STone solution, and get the desired project from the Projects array contained in the Solution class:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Cycle through all the projects contained in the solution for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": project.ActiveProjectConfiguration.Debug = True # ... Fields Field Data type Description Name string The name of the project configuration. NoLogo bool If true, suppress the display of startup banner and information message. Debug bool If true, enable debugger information on object file (breakpoint support). Coverage bool If true, enable code coverage information on object file. NoOpt bool If true, disable code optimization. NoOptIO bool If true, disable IO optimization. SubrangeCheckEditors bool If true, emit Subrange limits check instructions during Read operations in Protocols, NFC, etc.. SkipApplicationSigning bool If true, skip application signing. InheritMethodVisibility bool If true, inherit method visibility rather than using default visibility (protected). RepeatUntilExitsOnFalse bool If true, the REPEAT/UNTIL loop will exit when condition evaluation returns FALSE, behaving like a DO/WHILE loop. LongStrings bool If true, enable the usage of Long Strings, with length over 255. Configuration string The project ST configuration. Resource string The project ST resource. CustomFileDirectories string Custom file directories. PreprocessorDefinitions string Preprocessor definitions. UserParameters string User parameters. PreBuildCommandLine string Pre-build events command line. PostBuildCommandLine string Post-build events command line. Example: Disable InheritMethodVisibility on MyProject.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Disable InheritMethodVisibility on MyProject for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProject": project.ProjectConfiguration.InheritMethodVisibility = False # Save the solution stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Close()

help.title: Best Practices
help.officialContent:
Properties of a good unit test A good unit test possesses several important properties that contribute to its effectiveness and reliability.
Keep them in mind when writing your unit tests.
Unit tests should be:
Atomic
Unit tests should only test a single assumption about a small piece of functionality.
This assumption should focus on a behavior of the unit being tested. Therefore, multiple tests are necessary to check all of the assumptions for a given unit.
If you are testing multiple assumptions in a single test or calling multiple POUs in a single test, the scope of your unit test is probably too large.
Deterministic
Unit tests should be deterministic.
If no code changes are made, a good unit test should produce consistent results when executed multiple times, regardless of the test environment or order of execution.
The test should not rely on external factors that could introduce variability. A good unit test provides reliable and trustworthy feedback.
Automated and repeatable
The benefits of unit testing are fully realized when the execution of unit tests are automated and repeatable.
This will allow unit tests to be executed as part of a build process or CI/CD pipeline.
New developers should be able to just get the project and click on the button to run the tests without having to set anything up, regardless of which computer runs them.
Isolated and independent
A unit test should be isolated, meaning it tests a specific unit of code in isolation from other components or dependencies.
It focuses on a single piece of functionality, such as a method or function, without relying on external resources, connected devices, target type, global variables or interactions.
Each unit test should be independent of others, allowing them to be executed individually or in any order.
Tests should not rely on the execution or success of other tests, as this can lead to unpredictable results and difficulties in troubleshooting.
Easy to set up and implement
Unit tests should be easy to set up and implement.
If they are not, this is a symptom in the system that may indicate a larger problem.
The problem could be in the way that the unit being tested is designed or in the way that the test is being written.
Although we want a high amount of unit test coverage, we do not want developers to spend inordinate amounts of time writing a single unit test.
Unit tests should be easy to write.
Readable
Well-written unit tests use clear and descriptive names for test methods, making it easier for developers to understand the purpose of the test and the scenario being covered.
Additionally, they should have well-structured and readable code, with proper comments and documentation where necessary.
A good rule on the name of the test is to use the following pattern:
[POUNameUnderTest][Scenario][ExpectedBehavior]
For example, if you are testing a function called Add, you could name your test Add_WhenAddingTwoPositiveNumbers_ShouldReturnTheSum.
Fast
Unit tests should execute quickly, fast tests facilitate rapid feedback.
A complex software system that has adequate test coverage will have a large amount of unit tests.
The execution of unit tests should not slow down development processes (e.g. a CI/CD pipeline).
Based on the other desirable properties of unit tests, such as being atomic, isolated, and independent, they should execute quickly.
By adhering to these properties, developers can create unit tests that are reliable, efficient, and valuable in ensuring the correctness and stability of their codebase.

help.title: Commissioning
help.officialContent:
How to start with commissioning From View menu, select Commissioning to open an empty commissioning document editor
On top of the document,3 functions are available
Create new workspace creates a new workspace; Open workspace opens an existing workspace; Close workspace closes the current workspace. The commissioning document editor still open. Only the default configuration toolbar is visible; There are 4 modes for creating workspace
Project creates a new workspace from project compilation information(project need compile first). This opinion only shows when a project is opened. Parameter and Enum translations for all languages are automatically populated from translation editor. Application creates a new workspace from the given application binary containing only EN language Parameter and Enum translations. Commissioning creates a new workspace from the given .stc file containing commissioning information. Target creates a new workspace with commissioning information retrieved from the active target. Commissioning User Interface After create or open a workspace, the main view appears. It contains 4 areas:
Workspace toolbar shows all commands for a workspace; Navigation tree shows all contexts for a workspace; Context toolbar shows all commands for a specify context; Parameters data grid shows all parameters for a specify context; Tags shows all tags for a workspace; Workspace toolbar Workspace toolbar contains the main commands for a workspace
Create new workspace creates a new workspace; Open workspace opens an existing workspace; Open Binary opens a binary file compatible with current workspace, then user can modify the binary in Binary tab; Close workspace closes the current workspace; Refresh workspace refreshes the current workspace according to the commissioning info in controller; Export workspace creates a cloud content useful to other Service tools provided by Carel; Export for c.web exports the parameters in the right format can be import in c.web; Export for c.touch export the parameters in the right format can be import in c.touch. One file will be exported for each serial connection provided in the application; Export documentation file exports a csv file with the main information about the parameters. It is useful as entry point to create a custom documentation; Export package embed web pages and user files into a given .pack file. Then user have the possibility to install web pages and user files directly with the pack file. Steps： Choose an exist pack file. Only after select a pack file, user can goto next step. Choose web page folder. Choose user files. User can select multiple files or a folder (the folder could contain files and sub folders). There is an option “Clear user file folder on the controller” indicate whether clear user file folder when downloading the pack file into controller. The maximum size of the web page files and user files before compression is 80MB. Press Export button to embed the web pages and user files into the given pack and save as a new file. The maximum size of the exported pack file is 15MB. Login login to carel tenant to see the “Visibility” column on in Profiles; Navigation tree Navigation tree shows all contexts of the workspace. User can switch to different context by click on a navigation item.
Each navigation pane will list all the sub-items of a specify context.
Monitoring goes into Monitoring context, to watch parameters value; Configurations goes into Configuration context, to set parameters configuration value; Profiles goes into Configuration context, to design profiles; Descriptions goes into Description context, to edit parameters translations; Controller configurator goes into Controller configurator context, to edit simulator setting; Alarms goes into Alarms context, to check alarms; Binary goes into Binary context, to edit translations resources;need to open a .bin file Monitoring overview Once select the,Monitoring context from navigation tree, Monitoring view appears.
It contains a data grid with all the parameters and a live chart area to draw the value of the selected parameters.
The Monitoring feature need connect to a proper device.
When the device is connected, user can do these works:
Change parameter value in the data grid; Add parameters in the live chart drag the items from the data grid and drop it in the chart area; Disable the tracking of one parameter uncheck the flag of parameter in the box at the top of the chart; Delete the tracking of one parameter click twice on the parameter label in the box at the top of the chart; Once the device is disconnected, all the parameters in live chart will be removed; Monitoring toolbar allows user to:
Export value log exports all parameters value logs in a csv file. This option is available only when the device is connected; Save chart values saves the parameters sample values which drawn on the chart in a xml file. This option is available only when the device is connected and the live chart has at least one parameter; Clear chart values clears the old sample values and restart draw the chart. This option is available only when the device is connected and the live chart has at least one parameter; Clear series clear the selected parameters which drawn on the chart. This option is available only when the device is connected; Change colors for series change the colors for the selected parameters. This option is available only when the device is connected; Configurations overview In left navigation tree,Configurations pane list all the exist configuration items.
As default, there is a (None) configuration item. User can not edit the configuration value when this item is selected.
Configuration toolbar New configuration creates a new configuration; New cloned configuration creates a configuration with the settings of all the cloneable parameters. In a cloned configuration, it stores also the version of application firmware. All the values come from the running device. The configuration is read only, user can’t modify it. This option is available only when the device is connected; Remove configuration remove the selected configuration; Duplicate configuration creates a copy of the selected configuration; Clear configuration cleans all values of the selected configuration; Apply default values applies the default values in the selected configuration; Apply live values copies the running values in the selected configuration. This option is available only when the device is connected; Apply configuration applies the configuration to the connected device. This option is available only when the device is connected; Apply cloned configuration applies the cloned configuration to the connected device. Asking for the right pack with the firmware in case version are different. This option is available only when the device is connected; Import configuration imports an existing configuration; Export configuration exports the selected configuration in a .stconfiguration file. The configuration is encrypted, its values can be accessed only using Carel tools; Multi export configuration multi exports the names of selected configurations in a .stconfigurations file. Multi download downloads the selected configurations to target; Wipe folder Wipe destination folder; Compare configuration compares the selected configuration with another configuration; Cloning feature A cloned configuration save all the settings of the device useful to create a perfect clone of that. A clone configuration contains a set of parameter values but also the version of application. When user tries to apply a cloned configuration to a device, if in that is not running the right application version, need provide right pack for that. A cloned configuration is marked with the dedicated icon present for the cloned configuration in the navigation pane.
Compare feature When a configuration is selected, it can be compared with another one by pressing the Compare feature. The output is a dedicated view in which all the differences are highlighted in yellow. Only the source configuration can be modified.
Profiles overview In left navigation tree,Profiles pane list all the exist profile items.
In right side, a data grid list all the parameters. As default, it is in profiling mode. User can set parameters accessible property for a profile.
Profile toolbar Add profile creates a new profile; Remove profile remove the selected profile; Copy profile creates a copy of the selected profile; Edit profile popups a content to edit the selected profile; Import profile imports an existing profile; Export profile exports the selected profile in a .stprofile file. The file is encrypted, its values can be accessed only using Carel tools; Profiling allows to set parameter accessible in all existent profiles. The data grid shows all parameters and profiles columns. In the column with profile name, user can check or uncheck the checkbox to expose or hide the parameter for the profile; Multi download downloads the selected profiles to target; Wipe folder Wipe destination folder; Profile editing The profile editing popup content allows user to:
Set connection password associates a password parameter to the selected profile. When the Applica or Applica Desktop user tries to connect to the device with a password profile. The available password parameters are defined in Attribute wizard. If the password is a parameter, its value can be different in different devices. This approach ensure to specify different values of the password for the same profile. Set UI profile sets the selected profile as UI profile. A UI profile is marked with the dedicated icon in the navigation pane; Cloning protection defines an alphanumerical password for the selected profile. As said before, the cloning feature allows user to save the state of the machine and replicate it in other instances of the same application. It is a quite warning feature cause it’s quite powerful. So apply clone operation needs a quite strong control. With cloning password, the same profile can give to different users but only the user knows cloning password can do apply cloning operation. Rename profile sets a new name for the selected profile; Parameter visible The parameter is visible at runtime if and only if the variable in the visibility column is TRUE.Note that the visibility column can be used only after login.
Descriptions overview In left navigation tree,Descriptions pane list all the exist language keys. As default, there is a default item.
Description toolbar allows user to:
Add language creates a new language; Remove language remove the selected language; Language switch switch the language to download; Import translations imports translations from an existing file(.xlsx or .sti18N); Import from translation editor imports translations from translation editor(need open related STone project); Export translations exports all translations to a file(.xlsx or .sti18N); Download to target downloads the translations to target; Wipe folder Wipe destination folder; Tags overview In left navigation tree,Tags pane list all the exist tag items. In right side, there are the parameters which filtered by the selected tags.
User can filter parameters by click a tag item from the left navigation pane. User can add new custom tags simply typing in the tag column in data grid and remove one tag by click the x icon in the right of the tag label. More than one tags can be assigned to a same parameter.
Controller Configurator Overview In left navigation tree, Controller Configurator pane lists all the settings that can be sent to the target (or received).
Target settings are visible in controller configurator tab. Settings are divided by categories only for view purpose, “export” and “download” operations will save all the settings together. In this view user can:
Import from file. Import a .ini settings file from a folder. Export. Export a .ini settings file to a folder. Load default configuration file. Default settings will be imported. This will override the current settings. Upload from target. Upload the settings from target. This functionality is enabled only if target is connected. This will override the current settings. Target has to support file system management. Download to target. Download the settings to target. This functionality is enabled only if target is connected. This will override the current settings. Target has to support file system management. Download certificates. Download HTTPS or FTPS certificates to target. This functionality is visible only when Server section is selected, and enabled only if target is connected. Target has to support file system management. It is important to know that:
When the workspace is saved, STone also saves a settings.ini file in workspace folder. When a workspace is open, STone searches for a settings.ini file in the same folder. If found, the file will be imported automatically, otherwise a blank page will be shown. If the workspace is open, no settings have been imported yet (so there is a blank page) and user connects to the target, STone will try to upload settings automatically from target. The settings available are divided by categories:
Built-In: Backlight Timeout, Backlight Level, Buzzer Key (Enable/Disable).
ETH:
Device name, the max length of the device name is 63 characters IPv4 setting: DHCP (Enable/Disable), mDNS (Enable/Disable), IP, Subnet Mask, Gateway, DNS1, DNS2. IPv6 setting: Enable (Enable/Disable), DHCP v6 (Enable/Disable), Public IPv6, Class, Gateway IPv6, DNS IPv6. Firewall:
IPv4, the max rules configured is 4 IPv6, the max rules configured is 4 pLan:
pLAN Address Terminal address 1, Terminal shared 1 (Enable/Disable) Terminal address 2, Terminal shared 2 (Enable/Disable) Terminal address 3, Terminal shared 3 (Enable/Disable) Reboot Delay: Reboot delay (Seconds).
Server:
HTTP (Enable/Disable), HTTP port, HTTPS (Enable/Disable), HTTPS port, HTTPS certificate file and HTTPS certificate key file. FTP Mode(OFF/FTP+FTPS/FTPS Only), FTP port, FTPS certificate file and FTPS certificate key file. System Clock:
NTP (Enable/Disable) NTP server 1, the max length of NTP server 1 is 47 characters NTP server 2, the max length of NTP server 2 is 47 characters Poll Interval (Minutes) Timezone, the max length of timezone string is 80 characters USB: USB Mode(OFF/CDC/MTP), USB HOST (Pen Drive). Note that only one of CDC/MTP can be enabled.
Users: See paragraph below. Users section has some other functionalities:
Add user. A new user will be added. Name, password and Profile fields are mandatory. Password is encrypted. The max of user count is 5, the max length of password is 16 characters and the max length of profile name is 15 characters Add anonymous user. The reserved user “anonymous” will be added. This user has a default password and cannot be changed. Only one “anonymous” user can be added. Remove user. The selected user will be removed. Alarm Overview In Alarms tab we can find two lists of alarms, one for active alarms, one for history alarms. Lists are refreshed automatically when their values change. It is possible to reset those lists using the relative buttons “Clear active alarms” and “Clear history”. Those lists can also be exported in a .csv file with button “Export”. No information about alarms will be shown if the target is not connected.
Binary If workspace has a binary file associated or if a binary file is loaded by user, Binary tab will appear. STone will create a new .bin named like “XXX-v1.0.15-C#00000000-P#00000000-D#67E3D8F1.bin” when loading,and the changes will also be saved into this .bin file.
The main grid is the translations editor where the functionalities allowed are:
Add/remove languages Change font type Change font size Modify existing translations Functionalities available in binary toolbar are:
Language manager opens the language manager to control languages, font and size; Import imports a translations sheet; Export exports a translations sheet; Profiles embeds profiles; Configurations embeds configurations; Descriptions embeds descriptions; Download executes a full download to target; Binary size shows information about memory occupation expressed in KB and percentage; CRC shows binary CRC; Functionalities available in languageManager are:
Add add a new language; Remove remove a language; MoveUp move up language; MoveDown move down language; Save save language changes; How to add a Spark file in project In order to add a Spark file in project you need to:
Right click on project Open the sub menu Add > Commissioning > Create workspace In the dialog, insert the name of the Spark file (the dialog will propose the name <PROJECT_NAME>.spark) Click the OK button on dialog How to import an existing Spark file in project In order to import an existing Spark file in project you need to:
Right click on project Open the sub menu Add > Commissioning > Import workspace In the dialog, select the current existing Spark file Click the YES button on dialog

help.title: Custom Mask
help.officialContent:
Custom Mask UI Editor also provide a ST skill development way. To implement it:
Right click on a Loop and choose the Add Custom Mask item; Input the name of custom mask, Press OK button. A custom mask is being added in the active loop; Double click on that custom mask. A ST editor window appears, it already exists a stub of an ST function; Develop your mask logic with ST codes in that ST function; Stone runtime will call this ST function every program cycle to show the custom mask correctly. If a normal mask is not able to match the requirement in developing, and with high skill of ST development, user can write his own mask directly in ST codes.

help.title: DATE and TIME_OF_DAY type support
help.officialContent:
DATE and TIME_OF_DAY type support DATE and TIME_OF_DAY is supported as a read-only data type in UI Editor.
User can set “Default Date Format” property of UI Editor to get the proper default date format.
Moreover, using the API SetDatesFormat(DateFormat#YYYYMMDD); user can change at runtime the desired format.

help.officialContent:
Default target connection Table of default connection with target:
Line Configuration Target node Display serial 57600 8N1 1 Integrated serials 115200 8N2 248 Optional serials 19200 8N2 248 Warning If use Terminal detector, the pLan protocol is alternated with Modbus every 5-10 seconds (the code is customizable) in the display serial.

help.title: Editor
help.officialContent:
Translation Editor toolbar Functionalities available in translations editor are:
Language manager opens the language manager to control languages, font and size; Import imports a translations sheet; Export exports a translations sheet; Properties opens properties tab view; Add section adds a section; Remove section removes the selected section; Rename section renames the selected section; Add resource adds a resource in the selected section; Remove resource removes the selected resource; All/Embedded filter permits to select if all the sections should be visualized or only the embedded ones; Only used by variable filter toggle to show enum sections which only used by variable,only visible when enum section/category is selected; Translations Editor view Selecting a section we can see the relative resources. The first column is the resource name followed by the translations for each language. Enums have also the value column (INITVALUE).
The enum section type can be filtered for the variables used
The sections may or may not be embeddable;
embedding them as resources implies that the language can be changed at runtime via the API:
you can check which editor and where a translation is used.
Categories Sections are grouped by these categories:
Enums. Special fields. UI. Params. Other.

help.title: Export Loop UI
help.officialContent: Export Loop In UI Editor, a simple UI Documentation exporting feature has been developed. Just need right click on a Loop object in the tree view and select the “Export” item. A binary file(*.loop) will be created. It collects all the information of a Loop.

help.title: Field properties UI
help.officialContent:
Field Properties - Comment Actions User can define a set of actions for field level. The steps is the same described for global action. In case of a field action defined “over” a Mask, Loop or a global action, the priority gone to the Field one EnableOn With this property a Field can be enabled or not with any kind of a boolean expression. This means that the user can show or not a field coupling this property with a Boolean variable, a Boolean expression or a function with a Boolean result Min The minimum allowed value for the associated variable, this information is retrieved from variable list and user can’t modify it here. The variable list works as the single entry point to change this kind of information Max The max allowed value for the associated variable, this information is retrieved from variable list and user can’t modify it here. The variable list works as the single entry point to change this kind of information UsesTempVarContent With this property the user can decide if the change done with the key will be propagated at real time or when the cursor go to the next field.UsesTempVarContent = TRUE (default) The cursor is over the field and user press Arrow Up or Down to change the value. The new value is propagated to the application when the cursor go to the next field UsesTempVarContent = FALSE The cursor is over the field and user press Arrow Up or Down to change the value. The new value is propagated to the application after each Arrow Up or Down pushing Variable The associated variable Text (for Text only) It contains the text showed in the display You can edit or add new translation on this property via translation selection view.
If the section or key points to a resource that does not exist you will need to fix the value via the translation selection: Refer to translation selection Fieldtext User can use this property to associate a particular text with the variable in the display. The possible information to set is the text and the position in the display BoolStates(for Boolean vars) User can associate to a Text, a ScrollableText or an image one or both true and false Boolean value. When the application is running and the associated variable has the proper value, in the display will be showed the associated boolstate. If the variable type used for the field is an enum bool type, boolstate will be populated with translations of this enum, to manage translation see Translation editor.
i.e. FALSE -> “Off” TRUE -> “On” IntStates(for Integer vars) User can associate to a Text, a ScrollableText or an image one or more integer value. When the application is running and the associated variable has the proper value, in the display will be showed the associated intstate. If the variable type used for the field is an enum int type, intstate will be populated with translations of this enum, to manage translation see Translation editor.
i.e. 0 -> “Off” 1 -> “Low” 2 -> “Normal” 3 -> “High” IntPartDigitsCount(for real vars) It decides the number of the digit to show before the decimal point Precision(for real vars) It decides the number of the digit to show after the decimal point ZeroSuppression(for real vars) It decides if UI Editor shows or not the zero digits before the integer part Description (for Compact Field only) It represents the text showed in the display when the cursor is not on the compact field Fill(for Graphic object only) It allows to fill or not the graphic object Preview Value With this property variable value can show directly in the display area. This property is useful to show the multistate (int or Boolean) associated with the variable directly a design time Selectable With this property a Field can be selected or not with any kind of a boolean expression. This means that the user can make selectable or not a field coupling this property with a Boolean variable, a Boolean expression or a function with a Boolean result Show UoM If this flag is set to true, the display shows the UoM of the used variable. Otherwise it doesn’t show it Occupation(for Scrollable Text only) For Scrollable text, it represents the space occupied by the text. At runtime when the cursor is on the text, it moves toward left. Name It indicates the name of the mask Column The column position Row The row position SpecialField Groups several properties that can be reused in other datafields. (Selectable, EnableOn, ZeroSuppression, Precision, UsesTempVarContent, IntStates, BoolStates and actions)

help.title: Global actions UI
help.officialContent:
Global Actions At global level user can define some actions coupled with the pushing of one or more keys (where available)
Click in empty space of the Loop and Mask List tree view; Action node exist in the property grid. Expand the node, user can view all the defined actions and can add a new action or choose an existent one; In case of adding a new action, a new ST file will be generated. In this file, user can find a ready prototype of the new function.

help.title: Global properties UI
help.officialContent:
Global properties Click in empty space of the Loop and Mask List tree view.Property grid will show the global level properties.
These properties are useful to improve the UI editor experience
- Comment Default Date Format This property sets the default date format of DATE type variable shows on UI DefaultZone This property sets the Unit of Measure default zone used when the application is executed FixedZone If this flag is set to true, UI Editor handles only the default defined zone. This approach is suggested in order to manage only one zone and to have a small footprint. If it set to false, the application will be built with the entire UoM handling. In any case, the user can change at runtime this setting by using the API SetUIZone(zone); available in the Namespace System.Globalization MaskStackSize User can choose the deepness of the stack of the mask. More about the StackMask is described later Translation Handling This property is used to choose the way of translation generation. It can be set with two different values: GenerateForCurrentLanguage - The application will be generated with the current language. All the translations of the current language will be inserted inside of the generated ST code. This is the suggested way in case of a controller with low memory footprint EmbedLanguagesAsResource - The application will be generated with all the available translations and they will be stored as a chunk of binary data at the end of the binary code of the application. Using this approach the user can release all the available translations. In the future maybe the user can add a new translation for the application without re-compile the software. To do this a dedicated software must be developed

help.title: Graphic layout
help.officialContent: UI Editor Graphic Layout Loop and Mask List Shows a tree view that collect all the Loops and Masks information; Draw Area Display all the UI components; List of Mask’s (or Loop’s) field Shows all the objects used in the selected item (Loop or Mask). Fields List Shows all the possible fields that user can use to design the UI: - Comment Field A field is the “classic” variable container. Each time user drag and drop a variable of an elementary type a field will be created. It is the same concept expresses in 1tool and c.Suite Compact Field It is an innovative component. It has got the same feature of the field but when the cursor is not over the compact field, it shows a description instead of the value. Once the cursor is on the compact field, it shows the value and user can modify it. It is very useful for 7seg displays. Text It represents a text in the display Scrollable Text It represents a long text placed in a shorter place in the display. At runtime, when the cursor is on it, the text starts to move toward left and user can read it. Widget It is another innovative component. More Later about that Image User can place an image in the display, where supported Property Grid Displays all the information regarding the selected objects.

help.officialContent: Mask Properties - Comment Actions User can define a set of actions for mask level. The steps is the same described for global action. help.title: Masks' Stack
help.officialContent:
Masks’ Stack The movement across the masks of the application is ensured by a set of system functions: GoToNextMask(); GoToPreviousMask(); GoToMask(targetMask); There’s a mask stack which stores the last visited masks. There’re 2 functions to handle the mask stack: PushLastMask(); an internal instruction PopLastMask(); Anytime when UI editor navigates to an available mask, it push that mask at the top of mask stack. With the pop function, it’s possible to move to the last showed mask without know it’s name. And user can implement his own call stack.
Please pay attention: the default size of the mask stack is 10.User can change mask stack size in Global Property section
