help.title: Target
help.officialContent:
Target class This class contains all the APIs to manage a target, so it is possible to download, restart the target, read from and write to variables, use device recovery, etc…
Target class is part of the stone object which is already present when running the python script.
Except for device recover, the APIs works for both pc simulator and physical controller.
Fields Field Data type Description Watches Array[Watch] List of all successfully created watches. Tasks (Array[Task], Result) Tuple with a list of all tasks present in the target and a result instance. The list of all tasks is a Task instance. The result instance containing some information if the list cannot be retrieved. ActiveTask (Task, Result) Tuple with a the active tasks present in the target and a result instance. The active tasks are in a Task instance. The result instance containing some information if the list cannot be retrieved. WorkingDirectory string String with the current Working Directory of the simulator process Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
StartSimulator()Description:
Starts the “PC-Simulator” target with the settings of “STone IDE > Tools > Options > Simulation”.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() StopSimulator()Description:
Stops the “PC-Simulator” target
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Stops the pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() Connect(connectionString)Description:
Opens a connection to the target via the specified connectionString.
Returns:
True if successful and connected, false otherwise or if a connection already exists.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description connectionString string The Connection string to the target.
e.g. “TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122” or “Serial,COM11,1152008N1,248” for serial. Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") Disconnect()Description:
Closes the currently open connection.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Disconnect from the pc-simulator stone.Target.Disconnect() Restart()Description:
Restarts the target it is currently connected to.
Note: A connection has to be previously established with the Connect API.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Example:
# Connect to already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Connect("TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Restarts the pc-simulator stone.Target.Restart() Download(projectName, connectionString)Description:
Downloads the previous build to the currently connected target.
Notes:
The connection to the target, if open, must first be closed with the Disconnect API.
The solution must be opened with the Solution.Open API first. A build has to be performed with the Solution.Build API first.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description projectName string The name of the project of the currently open (not the name of the solution) to be downloaded.
e.g. “pCOProject1” connectionString string The Connection string to the target.
e.g. “TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122” or “Serial,COM11,1152008N1,248” for serial. Example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the already running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") CreateWatch(VarToRead)Description:
Creates a Watch object to read from and write to application variables.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description variable string The name of the variable to watch (with namespaces if any) the same as watches view in STone IDE.
e.g. “MySetPoint”, “MainInstance.MyFunctionBlock.MySetPoint”. Returns:
Returns a tuple of a Watch object and a Result object.
Example:
ST example:
VAR_GLOBAL MyVar: INT := 1234; END_VAR PROGRAM Main MyVar := MyVar; END_PROGRAM IronPython example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (my_var, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MyVar") if result.IsSuccessful: # Read from variable MyVar (value, result) = my_var.ReadValue() print(value) # Output 1234 # Write to variable MyVar, set value 5678 my_var.WriteValue("5678") # Read from variable MyVar (value, result) = my_var.ReadValue() print(value) # Output 5678 StartStopDeviceRecover(comPort)Description:
Starts or Stops the device recover on the specified comPort.
Tip: It is advisable to put a delay between two calls of StartStopDeviceRecover API to allow the controller to be switched off and on again.
Returns:
True if successful, false otherwise.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description comPort string The COM port of the controller.
e.g. “COM4”. Example:
# Starts DeviceRecover on COM11 stone.Target.StartStopDeviceRecover("COM11") # Stops DeviceRecover on COM11 stone.Target.StartStopDeviceRecover("COM11") ClearBinaries()Description:
Clears the currently downloaded application binaries from the target.
Returns:
void, no return value.
Example:
# Stops the pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() stone.Target.ClearBinaries()

help.title: Unicode character support
help.officialContent:
Unicode character support STone supports unicode characters in its ui elements. And normally when it is enabled, all the character size are not fixed, that means users should control it themselves. And the default size is 9, that holds 2 rows and 2 columns per character.
Below are ui elements supported:
Text ScrollableText FieldText Compact Field TextArea Multistates Tips: Be careful that if translatable property not checked, the unicode character would not display correctly for languages that not support unicode characters. This rule is applied on Text, ScrollableText and TextArea After the project built, the font and characters which are used would be auto-generated into a .stfont file under Gui folder. And don’t modify or delete it manually as it would break the correct work flow. How to use this feature? Add a language which support unicode characters.
Click Translations Editor. Add a language for instance ZH. Configure the font family and font size, default is SimSun and 9. Switch to current language to the new added one ZH. Unicode on Text
Add a new Text with some unicode characters like “中文”. Unicode on ScrollableText Add a new ScrollableText with some unicode characters like “中文”. Adjust the length for the unicode text under current language. Be aware that the length could not be greater than the minimum length for the different languages. For example, under language “ZH” the length of “中文” is 2 and under language “EN” the length of “English” is 7, so the ScrollableText length is not greater than 2. Unicode on FieldText Add a integer or boolean variable named “test”. Add a new Field to the terminal. Select the Field on the terminal, switch to property grid, edit the FieldText property with some characters like “中文”. Unicode on Compact Field Add a integer or boolean variable name “test”. Add a new Compact Field to the terminal. Input some unicode characters like “中文” Otherwise, select the Compact Field on the terminal, switch to property grid, edit the Description property with some characters like “中文”. Unicode on TextArea Add a new TextArea to the terminal with some unicode characters like “中文” Be aware that to display the unicode characters correctly, must manually adjust the size of TextArea. Unicode on Multistates Add a integer variable name “test”. Add a new Field to the terminal. Select the Field on the terminal, switch to property grid, edit the IntStates property with some characters like, make sure that unicode character works when resource type is Text: Value 0 -> 中文 Value 1 -> 测试 Input the Preview Value to check the display. For BoolStates, just follow the same step.

help.title: Widget UI
help.officialContent:
Widget Widget is a brand-new object introduced in UI Editor.
It is very powerful and it allows user to develop and create a powerful and ergonomic UI by writing ST codes. Moreover it enabling a fully re-using of the code, user can put widget in some libraries and speed up the UI creation. What is a widget? It is an ST class with some easy rules to observe useful to UI Editor to understand what user wants. How to create a widget? In the Project context menu (Solution Exploer) just select “Add/User Interface/Add Widget Template”. Change the metadata SUPPORT_TERMINALS according to the correct display type (“pGD1” or “SevenSegments” or “SevenSegments;pGD1”) A class to be a widget usable by the UI must respect some fixed rules: must use the METADATA WIDGET_TYPE and SUPPORT_TERMINALS must extend the BaseWidget class must have the public Draw() method it must have 2 variables called x and y of type INT for positioning in the form Once these rules are respected, the widget will be usable by the UI. Metadata are additional information of the class needed by the UI editor Metadata OCCUPATION is used to describe the UI occupation of the widget component Metadata GRAPHIC_COMPONENT is used to draw a preview of the widget (which, however, does not reflect the actual result in the target display). This metadata can be repeated multiple times to draw more complex graphic components. The values express: Type of shape; Relative size; Xoffset; Yoffset; Angle in radians Thanks to the BindableVariable (System.util.BindableVariable) it is possible to read and modify user variables within a widget, thus solving the problem of the modification / reading of user variables by the widget. Bind() method can be used to bind the variable to the widget (one off), TryGet()/Set() to get and set the value. In order to translate a widget, add a new section node in the lang file. In the section node, just add all the resources needed. On ST side, translation can be retrieved via GetLanguageString() API, passing the corrisponding Assets.Language as argument; the return value is the translated string.

help.title: Automatic Test
help.officialContent:
Base concepts - - Step It is the atomic part of the test. It uses the handles of STone to read and write the variable in the solution.
Every step has an icon for a quickly identification. Read, write, conditional jump, lock, unlock and file import are only some of the implemented steps in the Automatic Test feature. Test case It collects the steps. It could be used as a container of simple and reusable logic. Test suite It collects test cases.
It is the scope of the test.
It does not know the existence of the other test suite.
It could be represented as a flow chart. Test definition It is the file “.stat” included in the STone solution.
It is the main container and collects the test suites. User interface The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the test.
Navigation tree Step list Step editor Test execution result Property grid Navigation tree It shows the test suites and cases using a tree structure.
The test suites have the icon: . Near by the name there is the counter of the collected test cases.
The test cases have the icon: . Near by the name, there is the counter of the collected steps.
On top of the navigation tree there is the toolbar, it can be used to:
Create a test suite Create a test case Remove an item of the navigation tree Run selected test case Stop the execution of the running test It is possible to create a test suite or case using the right key of the mouse in a empty area of the navigation tree.
Step list Near by the navigation tree there is the step list.
It will be visible when will be clicked a test case in the navigation tree.
In this section we can be found:
the toolbar to modify the test case Filters to search steps Step list Toolbar Add a step
Remove selected steps.
Move up/down selected step.
Duplicate selected step.
Filters Search a step by title or description.
Filter steps by type.
Step editor There is a custom editor for each steps
Test execution result When a test execution will be finished, the section will collect the executed steps.
Every row will show id the step finished correctly or not, in case of error will be reported a message.
After a double click on a row, the step will be displayed.
Property grid Using the property grid, it is possible to edit the information about the test suite and case.
Create a test Create a test definition After creating a STone project, it is possible to add a test definition.
Click the right key of mouse on the name of the project, Add -> Tests -> Add Automatic Test Editor.
In the solution will be created the file “AutomaticTest.stat” and will be opened the editor.
Create a test case First at all it is necessary to create a test suite and at least one test case.
So, right click on an empty area of tree navigation and click “Add test suite”.
After that, selected the created test suite, right click on it and click “Add test case”.
It is possible to edit the property of test suite and case using the property grid.
The editable properties of the test suite are name and description.
The editable properties of the test case are:
Name Description Reset: means if do an application reset on the application startup Delay between steps: it is the time to wait between the steps execution On failure: it is the behavior to apply when a test fails its execution. The values are “StopTest” and “Continue”, to stop the execution of the test and the to continue the execution. Create steps To create a step, click the button “Add new step” in the step list and select the type of step.
Step editor Check step It validates a condition.
The condition check a set of variables.
The available variables checks are: =, <, >, <=, >=, !=.
It will be created complex conditions:
var1 > 0 AND var2=10 AND … var1 > 0 OR var2=10 OR … NOT(var1 > 0 AND var2=10 AND …) NOT(var1 > 0 OR var2=10 OR …) The field “evaluation type” specify how the condition will be evaluated:
And: every condition must be verified. Or: at least one condition must be verified NotAnd: the negation of “And” result. NotOr: the negation of “Or” result. Reset step It resets the test step.
Import step It edits the values of variables, which trend id defined in a CSV file.
Every assignitions will be every 500 ms.
If Synchoronous import checked, it will import the file in current task synchoronously, otherwise it will start an asynchoronous task to import.
The structure of the CSV file is:
Every column collects the trend of a variable The first cell contains the name of the variable to edit The following cells contain the value to write Every cells must be valorized This is a CSV example:
u[1].r u[2].r u[3].r u[4].r u[5].r 20 20 20 5 20 20 20.3 20 5 20 20 20.6 20 5 20 20 20.9 20 5 20 20 21.2 20 5 20 20 21.5 20 5 20 20 21.8 20 5 20 20 22.1 20 5 20 20 22.4 20 5 20 If the user want to compose the .csv file by hand using a text editor such as Notepad, he could use comma or semicolon. Both in the data and in the excel select the corresponding delimiter, for example:
1.If user selects comma as delimiter in excel, he should use comma in the text editor.
2.If user selects semicolon as delimiter in excel, he should use semicolon in the text editor.
Jump step It evaluates the condition and, if it is verified, jumps to a step.
It the condition is no verified, will be execute the next step.
If Unconditional jump checked, it will always jump and ignore the condition.
Lock step Lock variable writes.
Reference step Execute the target test case and return back to the caller step.
Unlock step Unlock variable writes.
Wait step It stops the execution of the test.
Wait until step It stop the execution of the step while the condition is verified.
It is possible to set the max time to wait/stop.
If the condition is not verified before the time limit, the step will fail.
Write step It edits the variables values.
It is possible to set a point value or increment the value.
Note The variables used in the test must be existed in the STone project and must be compiled.
To run a test, the solution will be downloaded in a target and STone will be connected.

help.title: Integrates with CI/CD (DevOps)
help.officialContent:
CI/CD is a set of practices and tools that enable the automation of building, testing, and deploying software changes.
STone IDE’s Unit Tests are designed with CI/CD (DevOps) integrations in mind, allowing seamless incorporation into the development and deployment pipeline.
When it comes to unit testing, CI/CD integration involves automating the execution of unit tests as part of the CI/CD process.
This ensures that the code changes made by developers do not introduce regressions or break existing functionality.
Integrating Unit Tests into the CI/CD pipeline provides immediate feedback on the status of tests, developers can catch issues early in the development process enabling them to quickly iterate and fix issues.
It promotes a culture of automated testing and helps ensure the overall stability and quality of the software being developed.
Unit Tests execution can be automated through the use of SToneCLI.
SToneCLI is a Command Line Interface (CLI) with, among other features, the unit-tests command to run unit tests and analyze code coverage.
It is possible to set a minimum required coverage percentage, when the total coverage is below the desired threshold the CLI execution will fail, alerting the developers.
It is also possible to generate log files in common format (JUnit, Cobertura) compatible with common CI/CD platforms.
Overall, the CI/CD integration of Unit Tests facilitates a smooth workflow by automating the execution of tests, ensuring adequate code coverage, and integrating testing into the larger development and deployment process.
SToneCLI Unit Tests commands Within SToneCLI it is possible to use the unit-tests command to run and optionally analyze code coverage.
cd "C:\Program Files (x86)\CAREL\STone" SToneCLI.exe unit-tests -s "C:\Path\to\solution.stone" -p "ProjectName" -r "report.xml" -c "coverage.xml" -m "70" -n "TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122" --code-coverage Parameter Required / Optional Description -s Required The path to STone solution file. -p Required The name of the project to build and download. -r Optional Report file path. If specified, a Junit report file will be created in the desired path. --code-coverage Optional (Default: False) Enables: Analyze Code Coverage. -c Optional, must enable code coverage Code Coverage report file path. If specified, a Cobertura report file will be created in the desired path. -m Optional, must enable code coverage Minimum Code Coverage. If specified, if the total Code Coverage is less than the desired value the execution fails. --log-level Optional (Default: Normal) [ Verbose | Normal | Quiet ], Verbose: all information, Normal: normal information and errors, Quiet: only errors. -n Optional Connection string to the target SToneCLI exit codes for unit-tests command Exit Code Description 0 No errors (All Tests Passed). -1 Invalid STone license. -2 Solution path file not found. -3 Failed to load solution. -4 Project not found. -5 Project build fails. -6 Unit Tests build fails. -7 Unit Tests not found. -8 Connection fails. -9 Download fails. -10 Tests execution failed. -11 Unknown error. -12 Code Coverage less than minimum.

help.title: Watch
help.officialContent:
Watch class This class contains all the APIs to manage a watch, so it is possible to read from and write to values of a connected target.
To read and write values a valid target must be already connected with matching sources with an opened solution.
Watch is part of the Target class.
Target contains an array of all the watches created (see more in the “Target” page).
Watch class is also returned from the CreateWatch() API of Target class.
Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
ReadValue()Description:
Read the value of a variable from the connected target.
Returns:
Returns a tuple of a string (with variable value) and a Result object.
The string will be empty if no read could be performed.
Example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (set_point, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MySetPoint") # Read from variable MySetPoint (value, result) = set_point.ReadValue() # Stops pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator() WriteValue(value)Description:
Write a value to a variable of the connected target.
Parameters:
Parameter Data type Description value string The value to be written.
e.g. “12”. Returns:
Returns a Result object.
Example:
# Open the stone solution and build stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "pGD1Prj1" project to the running pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("pGD1Prj1", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Create object watch (set_point, result) = stone.Target.CreateWatch("MySetPoint") # Write 12 to variable MySetPoint result = set_point.WriteValue("12") # Stops pc-simulator stone.Target.StopSimulator()

help.title: Regression Test
help.officialContent:
Base concepts The regression testing feature improves the user capability to test the application in an automatic way.
User can record a stimulus-file and use this file as the input to test the application automatically.
Regression testing have a Recording phase and an Execution Phase.
The first one is hand made(using for example a hardware simulator) to record a correct behavior.
The second one applies the values recorded in the first phase. Then the values of the first and the second phase are compared.
- Comment RegressionTest It is the atomic part of the test. It uses the handles of STone to read and write the variable in the solution. Test suite It is the scope of the test. It contains several regression test. It does not know the existence of the other test suite. Regression definition It is the file “.strt” included in the STone solution. It is the main container and collects all the test suites. User Interface The UI permits to have the control of all single parts of the test.
Navigation tree Test variable definition Property grid Navigation tree Navigation tree has 2 areas:
Definition: It shows the test suites and regression test using a tree structure.
A test suite have the icon: A regression test have the icon: On top of the Definition navigation tree, there is the toolbar, user can:
Create a test suite Remove a test suite Create a regression test Remove a regression test Show regression test properties Clone a regression test Record a regression test Execution: It shows all the batch execution items in a list.
A batch execution item may contains results for several test suites
On top of the Execution list, there is the toolbar, user can: Create a new batch execution item Remove an exist batch execution item Right click on a batch execution item, user can:
Show property of the selected item, allow to edit name property Create a new batch execution item from the selected one, this will clone the chosen recording tests quickly Remove the selected item from list Variable list Near by the navigation tree, there is the variable list. It is visible when click on a regression test.
In this section, user can define the variables of the regression test. There’re 3 kinds variables.
Input: Input type variables are the input materials of a test.
Test will read their value during Recording phase and apply their value during Execution phase. Output: Output type variables are for comparing.
Test will record their value during Recording phase and also get their value during Execution phase.
Then compare these 2 values, if the recorded value and the executed value are different(in the same program loop), execution result is considered as Failed. Status: Status type variables are used for initialization.
They are only read once before recording, and also set once before execute a test. It’s useful to set up a device. Property grid Show the properties of test suite or regression test, allow user to edit the property value.
Create a test Create a Regression testing editor After creating a STone project, it is be possible to add a regression testing editor.
Right click on the project node, then select “Add” -> “Add Regression Testing editor” item.
A “RegressionTesting.strt” file will be added in the solution and the editor is opened.
Create a regression test First at all it is necessary to create a test suite and at least one regression test in the suite.
So, first click the “Add test suite” button from toolbar.
After that, select the created test suite, and click the “Add regression test” button from toolbar.
It is possible to edit the property of test suite and regression test using the property grid.
The only property of a test suite is Name
The properties of the regression test are:
Name: meaningful Name of the regression test Delay: the delay time before start a test Skip restart: skip restart test Creation Date and Time: creation time information of the test. Readonly Portability available: if the regression test is portable in commissioning tools Variable Definition How to define test variables:
Select a regression test item, to show the variable definition list To add a variable, click the “Add variable” button from toolbar, then choose your interested variable from list To remove a variable, click the “Remove variable” button from toolbar Change the kind of test variable:Input, Output, Status Note: The variables used in the regression test must be existed in STone project and must be compiled.
Clone test Press “Clone test” button from toolbar, to full copy a regression test configuration: variaible definition, regression test properties.
After clone operation, a new regression test instance will be added under the test suite.
Record regression test Press “Record regression test” button from toolbar. A new window will popup, it split variables in 3 lists according to the variable kind. At beginning, the 3 variable lists are empty. Press “Record” button on the right-bottom corner, to start recording test. Your defined variables and the default channels will be added into the corresponding variable list. It’ll also display and update variables’ real time value correctly. Press “Stop” button on the right-bottom corner, to stop recording test. After recording finished, the regression test icon will change to User can not edit variables after a regression test is recorded. But he can clone a new regression test from the recorded test, he can also record a new test to overwrite the exist one.
Execute test Click the “Execution” toggle button from navigation tree Press “New batch execution” button from toolbar. It will popup a new window and list all the recorded regression tests. In the “Execution wizard” window, choose to be verify tests. Here you can also edit the batch execution name. Press “Next” button. It will list all your chosen tests in a tree view. Press “Start” button to start execution. Execute regression test one by one, and update the execution result in tree view.
After all tests executed, the execution wizard window close automatically. A new execution item will be added in the navigation tree. User can select the execution item to check the result. He can also export the result to a .csv file, it stores the detail variable values during the execution.
Note To run a test, the solution must be downloaded into a target first and STone will connect to the target to handle the variable.

help.title: Task
help.officialContent:
Task class This class contains all the APIs to get some information of the task present in the target, so it is possible to get the name, the status, the error message and the relative callstack, finally it can get and set if this is the active task.
Task is part of the Target class. Target contains an array of all the Tasks present in the Target (see more in the “Target” page) and a direct reference to the active Task.
The APIs works for both pc simulator and physical controller.
Fields Field Data type Description Name string Name of this task. Status string Status of this task. ErrorCode int If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the error code, otherwise 0. ErrorMessage string If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the error message, otherwise it is an empty string. Active bool “true” if this is the Active task, “false” otherwise. CallStack Array[string] If the status of this task is Error, this field contains the stack trace. The following is a non-exhaustive list of possible Status:
“Undefined” “Error” “OnCreation” “Stopped” “Running” “RunningStep” “RunningStepOver” “RunningStepOut” “Break” “Deleted” “Waiting” “Resumed” Example: Search for open libraries and close them.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Get the active task (activeTask, result) = stone.Target.ActiveTask # Print the name active task if(result.IsSuccessful): print(activeTask.Name) stone.Target.StopSimulator() Methods Below is the list of class methods, click on the name to read their documentation.
SetActive()Description:
Set this task as the active task.
Returns:
True if we change the Active task, false otherwise.
Example:
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Search for "MyProjectName" then add IAQ_v.1.0.0 library and Main.st file for project in stone.Solution.Projects: if project.Name == "MyProjectName": project.AddLibrary("C:\\Path\\To\\Lib\\IAQ_v.1.0.0.stlib") project.AddFile("C:\\Path\\To\\File\\Main.st", "Sources\\Programs") # Set "MyProjectName" as the active project, then save and build stone.Solution.SetActiveProject("MyProjectName") stone.Solution.Save() stone.Solution.Build() # Starts pc-simulator stone.Target.StartSimulator() # Download "MyProjectName" to the pc-simulator stone.Target.Download("MyProjectName", "TcpIp,127.0.0.1,4122") # Get all task (tasks, result) = stone.Target.Tasks # Change the active task if(result.IsSuccessful): for task in tasks: if task.Name == "IEC_TaskName": task.SetActive() # Check if the active task is changed (activeTask, activeResult) = stone.Target.ActiveTask # Print the name of the new task if(activeResult.IsSuccessful): print(activeTask.Name) stone.Target.StopSimulator()

help.title: I/O Management
help.officialContent:
I/O according to IEC 61131-3 The direct representation is the description of how a variable is associated to I/O Driver, accordinlgy to the purpose of the variable itself.
In order to represent the variable in a direct representation it must be used a concatenation of:
a percent sign “%” or “AT%” as Header mark location prefixed I,Q or M, where: I stands for Input thus if a variable is used to read the value incoming Q stands for Output thus if a variable is used to write the managed value M stands for Memory thus if a variable is pointing to another memory area a size prefix X (or none), B,W,D or L depending to the type of the variable (see the table below) one or more (see below hierarchical addressing) unsigned integers that shall be separated by periods “.” Type Size X 1 bit B 1 byte W 2 byte D 4 byte L 8 byte Example of a variable pointing to a Memory area %MW1.7.9 The implementer shall specify the correspondence between the direct representation of a varialbe and the physical or logical location of the addressed item in memory, input or output.
EXAMPLE Hierarchical address %IW2.5.7.1 For instance, reading from right to left, this variable represents the first “channel” (word) of the seventh “module”
in the fifth “rack” of the second “I/O bus” of a programmable controller system. The maximym number of levels of hierarchical addressing is Implementer specific
STone Approach Inside STone implementation of direct representation the % -variables provide an “abstraction layer” to isolate variables from physical driver.
For these reason the I/O Memory represent the chip I/O configuration respet the association of the variable with I and Q.
The image shows how the I/O variables are managed:
How to add the I/O configuration in STone How to start with I/O management to add I/O % variables just use the project context menu add I/O to project
The resulting operation will be the creation of the IO_Config.st, containing the declarations of the Global variables usefull to manage the I/O mapping.
VAR_GLOBAL U AT%IX1.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_U_CH] OF uChannel; Uout AT%QB1.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_U_CH] OF UINT; Y AT%QW21.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_Y_CH] OF UINT; NO AT%QB31.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_NO_CH] OF BOOL; ID AT%IB31.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_ID_CH] OF BOOL; uConfig AT%MX1.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_U_CH] OF uChannelConfig; yConfig AT%MX21.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_Y_CH] OF yChannelConfig; noConfig AT%MX31.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_NO_CH] OF noChannelConfig; virtU AT%M61.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_U_CH] OF BOOL; virtID AT%M71.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_ID_CH] OF BOOL; END_VAR Pay attention if U,NO,ID etc variable are not used in the application, they will be stripped by the compiler (to avoid this, disable I/O optimization in the project options; see below for further info).
Example with I/O configuration Example: configure third U channel as NTC uConfig[3].mode_sel:=LIB_IO_AIN; uConfig[3].mode_TYPE:=LIB_IO_PROBE_NTC; //very low filter uConfig[3].filter:=0;	//UI DrawString(REAL_TO_STRING(U[3].r),row,col); uConfig represent the configurations of the Universal channels. In this case we have configured the third one in order to have an Analog Input and as modality the reading of a ntc probe.
The filter parameter is the avarage of the last values read. Lower is ratio and less sensible will be the avarage to changes.
Example: configure 4th U channel as AOUT 0-10V (using STone I/O default declaration) uConfig[4].mode_sel := LIB_IO_OUT; uConfig[4].mode_type := LIB_IO_OUT_0_10V; Uout[4] := 1000;	Example: deplayed rele noConfig[1].mode_type:=LIB_IO_DELAYED_RELE; noConfig[1].tOn:=1000; noConfig[1].tOff:=3000; noConfig[1].enable := TRUE; noConfig[2].mode_type:=LIB_IO_DELAYED_RELE; noConfig[2].tOn:=1000; noConfig[2].tOff:=4000; noConfig[2].enable:= TRUE; noConfig[3].mode_type:=LIB_IO_DELAYED_RELE; noConfig[3].tOn:=1000; noConfig[3].tOff:=5000; noConfig[3].enable:= TRUE; % Advantages: configuration VS mapping The “power” of the “% variables” is that they always represent the inputs, the outputs and their HW configuration: we can observe the I/O HW configuration regardless of the software mapping which makes the application.
For example, looking at %I, %M is possible to detect if a probe is disconnected, without having to know the application variable which manages the error (if provided).
We could look I/O status from tera or from a local supervisor We can copy HW configuration coping %M array We can provide different set of SW mapping on the same application: since we use %, no memory is allocated We can well manage I/O U channel configurability, mapping different types of variable on the same % location I/O advanced management Y channel can be configured (5 ways) as usual with %M and output will use %Q values U channels can be configured as AIN, DIN, AOUT or counters or frequency meter using %M. Inputs map over %I, outputs over %Q NO channels can be configured as normal, timed or cyclic using %M. Timed NO channels can be grouped by an index. I/O and tasks Every task has its own input and output image: Inputs can’t change during execution Output will be sync at the end of the execution of the task Firmware takes care to: report task output changes to other tasks provide protection among accesses I/O default configuration U and Y channels are configured by default to “not used” (255 value in %M) Application can provide specific initial values (global variable definition) The I/O driver could detect this (using callback) providing the correct HW configuration before application starts I/O Virtualization We can easily provide Input Virtualization, disconnecting I/O driver from %I. In order to enable the virtualization of a i-th channel, just set true virtU or virtID for U or ID respectively. From a survey, we discover that it is important to provide input virtualization (output is less important) To virtualize a channel we always used %M as selector VAR_GLOBAL virtU AT%M61.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_U_CH] OF USINT; virtID AT%M71.0 : ARRAY[1..LIB_IO_MAX_ID_CH] OF USINT; END_VAR I/O API Added API support to manage asynchronous I/O: Input will be read when invoked Output will be applied when invoked Added API support to manage I/O event When a boolean input value changes: When an analog input crosses a threshold (with hysteresis) We implement a callback inside I/O driver when multiple read happens API for Chip I/O version (FW-HW) Advanced: disable I/O optimization (STone) The compiler keeps track of tasks that use I/O variables, avoiding to allocate memory mirrors for tasks that do not access the I/O (eg UI task, exception task). Obviously if the I/O variables are declared and not used in the application, in fact are not updated by any task and consequently the STone watch does not allow to change the physical states of the I/O. By enabling this option, these optimizations are not carried out, and the user can change the I/O status from the watch, without having to use variables in the UI or in the strategy. In short: if you have the need to make an I/O test without having to “use” variables, enable this option. Advanced: GroupID on delayed DOs To manage a “star delta” motor start, we need a precise sync between different Digital Outputs (DOs). On programmable platform, DO can be controlled by peripheral micros To be sure to activate all related DOs at the same time, we can use GroupID parameter on delayed DOs If you don’t care about this problems, just ignore the parameter (leave it to 0). In short: if you have delayed NO to manage, with time relationship among them, just group related DOs with the same number.

help.title: Result
help.officialContent:
Result class This class contains the information on the status of execution returned from some APIs, so it is possible to verify if the execution ended successfully and consult errors description if any.
Checking whether the execution of an API was successful can be done quickly by checking the value of the boolean field IsSuccessful of the Result class.
Result contains Errors, Warnings, Messages.
They are arrays of Note class.
Note class contains a string field called Description with more information of the execution of an API.
Fields Field Data type Description IsSuccessful bool True if API executed without errors, False otherwise. Errors Array[Note] List of all errors represented with Note class, if any. Warnings Array[Note] List of all warnings represented with Note class, if any. Messages Array[Note] List of all messages represented with Note class, if any. Example: Since Errors, Warnings and Messages are lists, you can cycle them with a for.
# Open the stone solution stone.Solution.Open("C:\\Path\\To\\Solution\\Solution.stone") # Build the solution result = stone.Solution.Build() # Print build errors, warnings and messages if build failed if not result.IsSuccessful: for error in result.Errors: print(error.Description) for warning in result.Warnings: print(warning.Description) for message in result.Messages: print(message.Description)

help.title: Shared Memory
help.officialContent:
General info The shared editor is used to manage the variables that needs to be shared among connected devices.
In order to share the variables inside the editor among devices, each project in each device needs to have the variables with data types in the same order, and also the same group id. Examples:
Example 1 Device 1 Device 2 These devices do not communicate because they have the same data types, but in different order.
Example 2 Device 1 Device 2 These devices communicate because they have the same data types in the same order, but if they don’t have the same Group Id, they cannot communicate.
In order to know if two devices can communicate (counting only the variables constraint), in the properties is present the “Shared editor id” that has to match among projects to share the memory.
The ids got by the “GetNetIndex()” method are setted as follow:
PLAN: The plan id UDP: An id starting from 1 assigned based on the devices UUID in ascending order (in the simulators the UUID is random) The ids are unique inside a network, indipendently from the group id (2 devices in the same network with different group ids, will have the GetNetIndex() as 1 and 2, instead of 1 for each device)
User interface There are 3 main parts in the shared editor.
Toolbar Variables list Properties Toolbar It contains a series of buttons in the upper left corner, and the info about the used editor variables and the used editor memory in the upper right corner.
Editor info In the upper right corner are shown the info about the variables inside the editor.
The first part show the number of variables used in the editor (400 variables is the limit).
The second part show the memory used by the variables inside the editor.
Buttons Remove variables - Remove the selected variables Go to index - Go to specific variable’s index [shortcut: ctrl + g] Move to index - Move the selected variables to the index furnished Import configuration - Import an editor configuration (ordered variables + groupId). There are two options of import: Append - Append the selected configuration to the actual (the groupId does not change from the current) Replace - Replace the current configuration with the selected ones Export configuration - Export the current configuration (ordered variables + groupId) Properties - Show the editor properties Shared Wizard - Initialize the ST Shared configuration Variables List Here is shown the list of variables ordered by index. Each variable show it index, the name and the data type.
The variables can be filtered by the table headers or, after the selection of them, they can be dragged and dropped, removed or moved to index through the toolbar or the context menu by right click.
Properties Here is shown the shared editor properties:
Group Id - The group where the variables are shared. (the manager must be set for each group) Shared editor ID - The CRC calculated with the variables indexes and the data types Shared ST Configurator The Shared ST Configurator dialog is a wizard allowing the user to ease the initialization of the Shared ST object.
The user instead of declaring the object and the initialization from the ST Editor, can follow the steps below and use the code in the ST editor.
Type the name wanted for the shared ST instance Change the Communication protocol desired Change the working mode as desired Manager: Performs communication checks and updates data of new devices Not Manager: Shares memory with other devices Automatic: A device in the shared network is set as Manager automatically. Copy the generated text consequently from the previous changes To use the wizard is required to open the shared editor as explained below.
Tips: the code block in the wizard is partial of the generated code, which is for the user’s invocation. For the other generated code, please check the file in ${ProjectDir}/Generated/Shared.g.st, something like below:
USING System.Net.Shared; VAR_GLOBAL Shared : SharedExt; END_VAR CLASS SharedExt EXTENDS System.Net.Shared.Shared METHOD PUBLIC Init : DINT Init := SUPER.Init(System.Net.Shared.Shared_Channel#PLAN, System.Net.Shared.Shared_Mode#Manager); END_METHOD END_CLASS Create shared editor After creating a STone project, click the right key of mouse on the name of the project, Add -> SharedEditor.
In the solution will be created the file “Shared.stshared” and will be opened the editor.
Add variables The shared editor accepts only elementary types and the only way to add the variables into the editor is from the Global Variables view.
Open the Global Variables view (usually at the bottom of the editor) and click on Editing in the Global Variables toolbar. Then, to add variables to the shared editor, you need to check the box of the variables you want to enable in the Shared column.
Remove variables In order to remove variables from the shared editor there are two ways:
From the Global Variables view From the shared editor Remove variables from GlobalVariables In order to remove variables from the shared editor you need to uncheck the box of the variables you want to remove in the Shared column.
Remove variables from context menu/toolbar In order to remove variables from the shared editor you need to select the variables you want to remove. Then you can remove them clicking the button in the toolbar.
Or you can remove them clicking the right button on any selected variable (or also the one you want to remove if it is only one) and then select from the context menu the Remove variables option.
Open properties In order to open the shared editor properties you need to click on the properties icon in the toolbar identified by a wrench icon, and then the properties will be shown in the property view.
Here you can view and edit the shared Group Id and view the Shared editor ID that has to be equal in the other project where you want to share the same variables.
Go to index In order to show the desired index without scrolling the whole variables list, there is the Go to index button inside the toolbar.
Clicking on it will show a popup in which you set the index you want to see, and then the selected index will be shown and be highlighted in the editor.
This feature is also accessible through the shortcut ctrl + g insted of the toolbar button.
Reorder variables In order to reorder the variables, instead of adding/removing them in order to reach the correct order, there are two ways to change the variables indexes.
Drag and drop Move to index through toolbar/contextMenu Drag and drop In order to move the variables using the drag-and-drop feature, you need to select the variables you want to move, then press the left click on one of them, and then release the click when you are over the position where you want to move the variables.
Move to index feature The variables can also be moved among indexes from the Move to index feature.
In order to use it, select the variables you want to move, then you can select the Move to index button from the toolbar, after that, in the popup that will be shown, set the index where you want to move the variables selected and its done. (the variable with the lowest index will be putted in the index selected, the others will be appended to it by the index order).
Instead of the toolbar button, you can right click on one of the selected variables (or also the one you want to remove if it is only one) and choose from the context menu the Move to index button.
Import/Export configuration The features export configuration and import configuration are useful when 2 devices with different projects needs to share some variables.
This feature spares you the waste of time on add and reordering the variables equally among projects.
Export configuration In order to export the configuration of the shared editor (sorted variables + group id) there is an option in the toolbar.
Click on it and in the dialog choose the location where you want to save the configuration.
Import configuration There are two availables option to import a configuration:
Append configuration Replace configuration Append configuration In order to append the configuration to the actual, you need to select the import configuration option, and from the dropdown menu, choose Append. When the dialog is shown, choose the configuration file you want to append.
The variables from the configuration selected will be appended to the actual variables in the shared editor in the same order as they are exported, and the Group Id of the project will not be imported.
Replace configuration In order to replace the actual configuration , you need to select the import configuration option, and from the dropdown menu, choose Replace. When the dialog is shown, choose the configuration file you want to import and replace to the current.
The variables from the selected configuration will replace the actual variables in the shared editor in the same order as they are exported, and the Group Id of the imported configuration will replace the one in the current project.
Note The variables used in the editor have to exist in the STone project and have to be compiled, otherwise they cannot be shared.

help.title: NFC
help.officialContent:
Enable the NFC To enable the NFC feature please add the NFC editor as follow:
Open the NFC configuration editor and start to add the variables from the proper button on the top-left corner.
Into the Global variables can be declared a new variable and shared to different configuration and thus modified inside the project.
And those variable which have been created from the global variable will be signalized with the global icon as follow:
NFC management Once the NFC editor has been composed, NFC has to be managed in the strategy:
NFC.Read() is used to get data from the device, without updating the binded variables NFC.GetData() causes an update (binded variables) NFC.Write() performs a write operation (values from binded variables to NFC) Here a very simple example:
VAR_GLOBAL force_Nfc_read : BOOL; force_nfc_get : BOOL; force_Nfc_write : BOOL; info : nfcInfo; END_VAR (******* CODE *******) NFC.Init(); (* NFC management *) GetNfcInfo(info); IF info.status = LIB_NFC_NO_PENDING_OPERATION THEN IF force_Nfc_read THEN IF NFC.Read()>=0 THEN force_Nfc_read := FALSE; force_nfc_get := TRUE; END_IF; ELSIF force_nfc_get THEN NFC.GetData(); force_nfc_get := FALSE; ELSIF force_Nfc_write THEN IF NFC.Write() >= 0 THEN force_Nfc_write := FALSE; END_IF; END_IF; END_IF; The GetNFcInfo() API will retrieve the status of NFC element, which can be:
nfcInfo : STRUCT (** status 0 OK, 1 pending read, 2 pending write, 3 no pending operation, negative values are errors*) status : DINT; (** ID of last request (progressive ID of request to read/write)*) last_request_id : DINT; The GetNfcWriteInfo() API is able to understand if a device is closed to the controller:
(* in order to get information about RF side (eg when a mobile phone is nearby) *) GetNfcWriteInfo(writeInfo); NFC Headers & Info NFC memory is organized in headers and block. Headers contain a lot of fixed information, managed by the firmware.
General header Field Size Description General header 6 Reserved General Header CRC 2 The cyclic redundancy check used to validate the content of header (CRC16) Device info header Field Size Description HEADER_VERSION 2 The version of the header SERIAL_NUMBER (CAREL UID) 8 The unique identifier of the hardware product FIRMWARE_VERSION 4 The version of runtime running on controller BOOTLOADER_VERSION 4 The version of boot loader running on controller HW CODE 2 Hardware code - Reserved MACHINE TYPE 2 Machine type - Reserved SPARE_BYTES 12 Free space for future definition filled with 0 CRC 2 The cyclic redundancy check used to validate the content of header (CRC16) OEM info header Field Size Description HEADER_VERSION 2 The version of the header OEM_ID 16 GUID of OEM (CAREL is a coded OEM) MACH_CODE 16 The product name assigned from the OEM (UTF-8) OV_OEM_ID 16 GUID of OEM OV_MACH_CODE 16 UTF-8 string of a brand string OEM_PRODUCTION_DATE 4 Free date of device of the unit OEM_FIELD_1 16 Free string #1 OEM_FIELD_2 16 Free string #2 OEM_FIELD_3 16 Free string #3 SPARE_BYTES 8 Free space for future definition filled with 0 CRC 2 The cyclic redundancy check used to validate the content of header (CRC16) Application header (STone) Field Size Description HEADER_VERSION 2 The version of the header PROJECT_ID 16 GUID that identify the project PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR 1 The major number of version of the project running on controller PROJECT_VERSION_MINOR 1 The minor number of version of the project running on controller PROJECT_VERSION_BUILD 1 The build number of version of the project running on controller PROJECT_VERSION_TYPE 1 The type character of version of the project running on controller GEOMETRY_ID 4 The value that identify of expected NFC memory map (crc) SPARE_BYTES 4 Free space for future definition filled with 0 CRC 2 The cyclic redundancy check used to validate the content of header (CRC16) Reserved header 96 Reserved header of 96 bytes for internal purpose Variable blocks This block contains variable values, followed by a crc. Suppose to bind 3 variable (INT DINT REAL) in NFC editor. Variable blocks Field Size Description variable1 2 Variable 1 INT variable2 4 Variable 2 DINT variable3 4 Variable 3 REAL CRC 2 The cyclic redundancy check used to validate the content of header (CRC16)

help.title: Python Integration
help.officialContent:
Base concepts STone provides a command line interface (SToneCLI.exe) to interact with some functionalities of the IDE, for example:
Build Automatic test Metadata generation Export workspace The CLI permits a Python integration using scripts.
The scripts can be usefull for continuous integration, continuous delivery and testing.
Following some snippet of Python scripts to call the CLI of STone using version >3.3
How to Here some simple steps to starting coding Python and calling “SToneCLI build”:
Using STone IDE create a project called “BaseProject2” in “C:\STone\Projects\” path Download and install Python version >3.3 Create file called “build.py” Open and edit the file using a text editor Paste the following code into the file: import subprocess import shlex def process_executor(exe: str, *args) -> int: command = '"' + exe + '"' + ' ' + ' '.join(args) print('Running command: ' + command) return subprocess.run(shlex.split(command)).returncode stone_cli = 'C:\\Program Files (x86)\\Carel\\STone\\SToneCLI.exe' process_executor(stone_cli, 'build', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"') Open a console Move to the folder containing the Python script Run the command: python.exe build.py Pay attention to SToneCLI.exe path and STone solution path.
It is possible to run and debug the script using IDE like Visual Studio Code or PyCharm.
In the next section will be explained the Python script.
Run executable The function “process_executor” runs an executable (as a subprocess) and returns the exit code.
import subprocess import shlex def process_executor(exe: str, *args) -> int: command = '"' + exe + '"' + ' ' + ' '.join(args) print('Running command: ' + command) return subprocess.run(shlex.split(command)).returncode Build To build a STone project use the follow command:
SToneCLI.exe build -s SOLUTION_FOLDER -p PROJECT_NAME -c CONFIGURATION_NAME Parameters Parameter Description -s Solution file path -p Project name -c Configuration name Example SToneCLI.exe build -s "C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone" -p BaseProject2 -c Debug Python Using Python:
process_executor(stone_cli, 'build', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"') Automatic test To run all the automatic test defined in a project:
SToneCLI.exe automatic-test -s SOLUTION_FOLDER -p PROJECT_NAME -c CONFIGURATION_NAME -n CONNECTION_STRING Parameters Parameter Description Solution file path -s Project name -p Configuration name -c Connection string to the target -n Example SToneCLI.exe automatic-test -s "C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone" -p BaseProject2 -c Debug -n TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122 Python Using Python:
process_executor(stone_cli, 'automatic-test', '-s', '"C:\\STone\\Projects\\BaseProject2\\BaseProject2.stone"', '-p', '"BaseProject2"', '-c', '"Debug"', '-n', '"TcpIp,10.10.9.128,4122"') Unit tests To run all the unit test defined in a project see Integrates with CI/CD (DevOps)
Metadata generation STone creates metadata file after build process in the output folder.
The file contains all the information about the project, some of these are:
Field name Type Example Description Project Version string “0.1.21” Project version ProjectName string “Heos Box CO2” Project name SolutionName string “HQ000HEOS00C0” Solution name Languages strings[] [“EN”] All the languages supported by the project UiLanguages objects {
“HEOneRow”: [“EN”],
“pGD1”: [“EN”]
} The languages supported by the project grouped by interface Hardware string “HEOS” The hardware supported by the project UserInterfaces strings[] [“SevenSegments”, “pGD1”] The interface supported by the project IdeVersion string “1.3.1.0” The version of STone Libraries object {

help.title: Terminal detector
help.officialContent:
Terminal detector Once the application is running, is possible to detect the type of terminal eventually connected.
Infact exist a special procedure within the serial 0, or known as Display port, that is
able to detect a terminal 7 segment or pGD1.
This automation switches between two main protocol from the first moments of the running application. This switch
is due to the different type of communication between 7segment and pGD1. Infact the pGD1 replies to the pLan protocol,
in particular to the getAvailableTerminal() API. After an amount of seconds, the protocol is replaced by another one able to speak with the 7 segment.
This procedure persist in time until one of the terminal replies or it comes to the polling status, if no terminal is replying again.
The algorithm then has some special cases:
it forces the line into pLan protocol in case there is the shared protocol active.
In the particular case where there is a commissioning tool connected to the shared serial0 (ModBus/pLan) this forces communication in ModBus preventing the pLan protocol from disconnecting the tool by disturbing the line with the token.

help.title: STone Help
help.officialContent:
File menu New project creates a new project; Close closes the current opened file; Close solution closes the current solution; Save active editor saves the current opened file; Save solution saves all files and configurations of the current active solution; Exit exits the program. File ➝ Open menu Open ➝ Solution opens an existing solution; Open ➝ File opens an existing file into the editor. File ➝ Recent solutions menu Recent solutions sub-menu displays a list of the most recent solutions opened with STone. This list is also available into the welcome page.
View menu Welcome page opens Welcome page docking window; Solution Explorer opens Solution Explorer docking window; Global variables opens Variable View for global variables docking window. Symbols opens Symbols docking window; Errors opens Errors docking window; Output opens Output docking window; Memory Occupation opens Memory Occupation docking window; Properties opens Properties docking window; Find and replace opens Find and replace docking window; Find results 1 opens Find results 1 docking window; Find results 2 opens Find results 2 docking window; Find symbols results opens Find symbols results docking window; Bookmarks opens Bookmarks docking window; Targets opens Targets docking window; Target Log opens Target Log docking window; Task monitor opens Task monitor docking window; System Errors opens System Errors docking window; IO Hardware Simulator opens IO Hardware Simulator docking window; Commissioning opens Commissioning docking window; Reset windows layout Reset windows layout to default setting. View ➝ ToolBars menu LoadSave shows solution load and save commands in main toolbar; Undo Redo shows Undo Redo commands in main toolbar; Cut Copy Paste shows Cut Copy Paste commands in main toolbar; Prev Next shows Previous Next position commands in main toolbar; View shows dock windows opening commands in main toolbar; Build shows all Build related commands in main toolbar; Simulator shows all Simulator related commands in main toolbar; Debug shows all Debug related commands in main toolbar; Text editor shows all Text editor related commands in main toolbar; Build menu Full build performs a complete build; Build for online changes performs a build of the POUs that contains changes; Batch build opens Batch build window, that could be used to perform multiple builds with different configurations with one click; Config manager opens Solution configuration manager window, that could be used to set different build configurations. Debug menu Start task starts the selected task, if it is not running; Break task breaks the selected task, if it is running; Stop task stops the selected task, if it is not stopped; Step into task steps into the current statement; Step over task steps over the current statement; Step out task steps out the current statement; Go to cursor go to the cursor focused statement; Set next statement set the next executed statement. Debug ➝ Windows menu Call stack opens Call stack window; Breakpoints opens Breakpoints window; Profiling opens Profiling window; Code coverage opens Code coverage window; Watch 1 opens the first Watch window; Watch 2 opens the second Watch window. Chart 1 opens the first Chart window; Chart 2 opens the second Chart window. Memory 1 opens the first Memory window; Memory 2 opens the second Memory window. Tools menu Start simulator starts the simulator if it is not running, stops it otherwise ( Stop simulator is displayed); Erase simulator binaries deletes all simulator binaries, in case of problem; Target System Update (Bootloader) opens a Target System Update window to perform a system update using Bootloader protocol; Target System Update (Package) opens a Target System Update window to create a binary package for upgrade device Firmware; Device recover opens a Device Recover window to force the default application sending a break the serial 0; Plugin Manager opens a Plugin Manager window to check or install plugin for Stone. Options shows Options window, where you can (first tab): change the Language change the Font type change the Font size change the Theme on the second tab you can change simulation setting: change the WebServer TCP-IP port change connection port for TCP-IP connection (PC side) map the device serial port on the PC port for the simulation set if the simulator must be stopped when STone is closed set if the simulator should stop on every error (even when STone is not connected to the simulator) set if the simulator should stop on subrange error (even when STone is not connected to the simulator) change the value of Time multiplier License opens a License Manager window to manage license for Stone. Tool ➝ Plugin Manager Install Plugin Tab** List all the install plugins.
Install new plugin by clicking + icon.
Tool ➝ License License Request** Need pass the HardwareID to carel administrator.
License Installed** If a license is installed, User can also update the license by click Update License button.
Target contextual menu (Disconnected target) Connect connects STone with the selected target if it is set as active target, and it is not connected - if not, replacing it there is the entry Set as active target. If the target is connected, Disconnect is shown; Start all tasks starts all the stopped tasks, if any; Stop all tasks stops all the running tasks, if any; Restart application restarts the application that is into the target; Download application changes performs an application download to the target, downloading only the POUs that results modified from the application running into the target.
Is possible to perform this functionality only if the target is not running a modified POU; Full download performs a download of the entire application, erasing the one into the target; Full download default application performs a download of the default application, erasing the one into the target; Update System allows to update the Operating system, the Bootloader, or both at the same time; Retrieve Application allows to upload from the target the running’s application (binary file); Snapshot allows to upload from the target the last one snapshot taken, if exists; Logs allows to upload from the target the logs, if exists; Signature info allows to upload from the target the signature information, if exists; Default connection info allows to upload from the target the default connection information, if exists; Production info allows to upload from the target the production information, if exists; Security allows to: Change Binary Password: this password is used to protect the binary application download; Change Connection Password: this password is used to protect the IDE connection; Rename target renames the selected target (only into targets list); Remove target removes the selected target from targets list, if it is not the active target; Properties shows the Properties window, where is possible to say some information and to set the connection type and its parameters. The Fire! and Hot Reload buttons Fire! button is a button that allows to save some steps. Fire! button builds the current solution, connects to the current active target if it is not connected (starts the simulator if the current active target is it, and if it is not running), and performs a Full download operation.
The Hot Reload button (near Fire! Button) builds and download to the active target only the POUs that contains changes.
Target Menu ➝ Update System Update OS and bootloader tab Choose one or both the .bin files to download into the target.
If the files are valid, the Update System button will appear.
Install the new firmware by clicking Update System button.
Follow the instructions that will appear on the screen.
Edit project It is possible to open “project editor” tab in the contextual menu of the project in solution explorer.
General Tab In “General” tab there are the following information:
Name: the name of the project File name: the absolute path to the project file Digital signature application certificate: path of certificate to sign the application Generate metadata file: enable or disable the generation of the file which collect the properties of the project.
Some properties are: Project version Project name Solution name Languages: the languages supported by the project Memories usage: ROM/RAM/NFC/Retain memory used by project in byte and percentage. Global variables: list of defined and compiled variables in the project. Symbols: list of defined and compiled symbols in the project. The file will be created in the output folder.
For for information about this functionality, see the section in Python Integration page. Build Tab In “Build” tab there are the following settings:
Project configuration: the project configuration to configure Target definition: the target the project is compiled for Suppress startup banner: hides the compiler startup banner in the output window or CLI during build Debug mode: allows to debug (place breakpoints) the built application Code coverage support: enables the code coverage support for the built application Disable code optimizations: disables the compiler optimizations (the application ROM footprint will be higher) Disable IO optimizations: allocates the IO memory also for unused IOs Subrange limits check in Protocols, NFC, etc.: emits the subranges checks into Read method call for Protocols, NFC, etc. Skip application signing: the application is not signed even if the certificate is set in the General tab Inherit method visibility: classes’ methods inherits the class visibility (enabled by default for old projects). If disabled (default for new projects) methods have PROTECTED visibility (if not specified) following IEC-61131 standard Configuration: the project configuration name to build Resource: the project resource name to build Preprocessor definitions: globally defined preprocessor definitions (equals to {DEFINE XYZ} or {DEFINE XYZ 0} statement) Output directory: output files directory

Examples USING System; USING System.UI; VAR_GLOBAL CONSTANT PAR1 : UDINT := 20; PAR2 : UDINT := 21; PAR3 : UDINT := 25; PAR4 : UDINT := 30; END_VAR VAR_GLOBAL bigData : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name : STRING := 'Device1'; password : STRING := 'Safe'; END_VAR PROGRAM main (*** Insert strategy here ***) VAR init : BOOL := TRUE; i : INT; tmpB : BYTE; tmpW : WORD; tmpDW : DWORD; bigData2 : ARRAY[0..1499] OF BYTE; name2 : STRING; str : STRING;	END_VAR IF init THEN FOR i:= 0 TO 1499 BY 1 DO bigData[i] := TO_BYTE(i MOD 50); END_FOR; init := FALSE; END_IF; (* Sets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 *) SetSettingB(PAR1, 25); (* Gets the BYTE setting with offset PAR1 and write this in tmpB *) GetSettingB(PAR1, tmpB); (* Sets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 *) SetSettingW(PAR2, 65000); (* Gets the WORD setting with offset PAR2 and write this in tmpW *) GetSettingW(PAR2, tmpW); (* Sets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 *) SetSettingDW(PAR3, 3000000000); (* Gets the DWORD setting with offset PAR3 and write this in tmpDW *) GetSettingDW(PAR3, tmpDW); (* Sets the settings with offset PAR4 *) SetSetting(PAR4, bigData); (* Gets the settings with offset PAR4 and write this in bigData2 *) GetSetting(PAR4, bigData2); (* Sets the current machine name *) SetNameSetting(name); (* Gets the current machine name *) GetNameSetting(name2); (* Sets the current Password settings *) SetPasswordSetting(password); (* Gets the current Password settings *) GetPasswordSetting(str); (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM FUNCTION ManageKey : BOOL VAR_INPUT keyPressed, keyCounter : UINT; END_VAR IF keyPressed = KEY_ENTER THEN (* Clears all settings from internal retained memory *) ClearSettings(); END_IF; (*** Insert UI here ***) ManageKey:=TRUE; END_FUNCTION ClearSystemSettings() System.ClearSystemSettings – Clears the system settings from internal retained memory.

+---------------------------+| System.USB.SetUsbHostMode || |System.USB.UsbHostMode-| mode |+---------------------------+Parameters Name Type Description mode System.USB.UsbHostMode - UsbDeviceMode System.USB.UsbDeviceMode – Usb device mode Members Name Description CdcMode Communication Device Class (CDC) mode: the USB port becomes a virtual serial port. MtpMode Media Transfer Protocol (MTP) mode: allows to transfer files to and from a Personal Computer. NoneMode USB device disabled Examples (* This example shows how to check the status of the connection with a USB device and how to set and get its mode, by choosing one of the following options: - CDC = Communication Device Class (virtual serial port) - MTP = Media Transfer Protocol (file transfer with a personal computer) - disabled *) USING System.UI; USING System.USB; VAR_GLOBAL mode : System.USB.UsbDeviceMode := UsbDeviceMode#NoneMode; device_ready : BOOL; error : BOOL := FALSE; END_VAR PROGRAM Main VAR current_mode : System.USB.UsbDeviceMode := UsbDeviceMode#NoneMode; result : BOOL; first_run : BOOL := TRUE; END_VAR; IF first_run THEN first_run := FALSE; (* Read the configured mode from the device *) System.USB.GetUsbDeviceMode(mode); END_IF; device_ready := System.USB.IsUsbDeviceReady(); (* The error, if present, must be manually removed from the UI *) IF error = FALSE THEN IF current_mode <> mode THEN current_mode := mode; (* Set the current mode, according to the UI *) result := System.USB.SetUsbDeviceMode(mode); IF result = FALSE THEN error := TRUE; ELSE error := FALSE; END_IF; END_IF; END_IF; (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM UsbHostMode System.USB.UsbHostMode – Usb host mode Members Name Description NoneMode USB host disabled MsdMode Mass Storage Device (MSD) mode: allows to transfer files to and from a USB pen drive. Examples (* This example shows how to implement the communication with a pen drive by setting the proper mode and checking if the drive is ready. Furthermore it shows how to write a file on the drive. *) USING System; USING System.UI; USING System.USB; USING System.FileSystem; USING System.Timer; VAR_GLOBAL info : System.SystemInfo; mode : System.USB.UsbHostMode := UsbHostMode#NoneMode; error : DINT(-20..9) := 0; write_file : USINT := 0; host_ready : BOOL; dateTime : System.Timer.DateTime; enableLabel : BOOL; END_VAR PROGRAM Main VAR current_mode : System.USB.UsbHostMode := UsbHostMode#NoneMode; result : BOOL; first_run : BOOL := TRUE; partition : System.FileSystem.Enums.PartitionType := System.FileSystem.Enums.PartitionType#PenDrive; filepath : STRING := 'test.txt'; openmode : System.FileSystem.Enums.FS_OpenMode := System.FileSystem.Enums.FS_OpenMode#OPEN_CREAT; file_id : DINT; written_bytes : DINT; text : STRING := 'test'; END_VAR; IF first_run THEN first_run := FALSE; (* Read the configured mode from the device *) System.USB.GetUsbHostMode(mode); END_IF; host_ready := System.USB.IsUsbHostReady(); System.Timer.GetTime(dateTime); IF dateTime.Second MOD 2 = 0 THEN enableLabel := TRUE; ELSE enableLabel := FALSE; END_IF; (* The error, if present, must be manually removed from the UI *) IF error = 0 THEN IF current_mode <> mode THEN current_mode := mode; (* Set the current mode, according to the UI *) result := System.USB.SetUsbHostMode(mode); IF result = FALSE THEN error := -1; ELSE error := 0; END_IF; END_IF; (* Check for a push of the PRG key to save a file on the pen drive *) IF mode = UsbHostMode#MsdMode THEN IF write_file = 1 THEN file_id := System.FileSystem.FileOpen(partition, filepath, openmode); IF file_id >= 0 THEN write_file := 2; ELSE write_file := 3; error := file_id; END_IF; ELSIF write_file = 2 THEN write_file := 3; written_bytes := System.FileSystem.FileWrite(file_id, text); IF written_bytes < 0 THEN error := written_bytes; ELSE error := 0; END_IF; ELSIF write_file = 3 THEN System.FileSystem.FileClose(file_id); END_IF; END_IF; END_IF; (* Refresh UI *) SendVirtualKey(NO_KEY, 1); END_PROGRAM FUNCTION set_write_file write_file := 1; error := 0; END_FUNCTION
